# -*- buffer-read-only: t; -*-
#+STARTUP: show2levels
* org-pwa
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: org-pwa
:END:

A mobile-first outliner for editing ~.org~ files in the browser. It works offline, needs no server and no account to use locally, and installs as a PWA.

This guide covers how to use it and, for anyone coming from Emacs, where it differs from real org-mode (see [[#differences-from-emacs-org-mode][Differences from Emacs org-mode]]).

** What org-pwa is (and isn't)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: what-org-pwa-is-and-isnt
:END:

org-pwa is a *touch-first outline editor*, not a port of Emacs. It reads and writes real ~.org~ files and keeps anything it doesn't understand exactly as written. Editing is built around tapping and gestures rather than Emacs keybindings, and it implements a useful subset of org-mode, not all of it.

It is not org-mode with full parity (babel in languages other than JavaScript, Emacs Lisp; see [[#known-limitations--not-built-yet][Known limitations]]). It is for opening a real org file on your phone, reorganizing the outline, checking off tasks, editing tables and saving back to disk, GitHub or a WebDAV server.

-----

** Getting started
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: getting-started
:END:

1. Open the app and tap *File → Open* if no file is open.
2. Choose where to open from:

   - *Local file*: the browser's file picker. Save writes straight back to the same file. Needs File System Access (Chrome or Edge on desktop and Android).
   - *GitHub*: browse a repo set up in Settings and tap a file. *Type a path instead…* is always there for a path the listing doesn't show.
   - *WebDAV*: the same, for a WebDAV server set up in Settings.
   - *Import file* (instead of *Local file* where File System Access is missing, such as iOS): reads a file once. Save downloads a new copy for you to put back (see [[#platform-support][Platform support]]).

3. Edit. Edits apply at once and are cached locally, so nothing is lost if you close the tab before saving.
4. Tap *Save* to write the file back to where it came from, or *Save As* to choose another destination.

*Menus and popups*: on a phone or tablet the menus and popups open as a bottom sheet. On a wide screen with a mouse the menus drop down under their button (*↑*, *↓*, *Home*, *End* and *Enter* move through them), and popups are centered dialogs. *Esc* closes either, and *Enter* accepts a question dialog such as a file path.

The modeline (see [[#modeline][Modeline and minibuffer]]) shows the filename, where it came from and whether it has unsaved edits. Once a second tab is open, the tab bar (see [[#tabs][Tabs]]) marks unsaved tabs with a dot.

-----

** Editing your outline
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editing-your-outline
:END:

- *Headings*: tap the title to show its actions: edit title, edit text, edit details (the general editor, below), add a sub-heading, TODO, move up and down, archive, attach (see [[#attachments][Attachments]]), delete, promote and demote. Most close the row after running; move and promote/demote stay open so you can repeat them. *Delete* always asks first, listing what would be lost, and every delete or discard confirmation in the app defaults to *Cancel*, so a stray Enter or tap never deletes. With a keyboard, the arrow keys move between the buttons and *Esc* closes the row.
- *TODO state*: tap the TODO badge to cycle the ~#+TODO:~ sequence (default ~TODO~, ~DONE~) one step at a time. The action menu's *TODO* button (~C-c C-t~) does the same, except that for a heading with no keyword in a file with more than one parallel ~#+TODO:~ workflow it opens a picker of every state of every workflow (see [[#progress-logging][Progress logging]]).
- *Fold and unfold*: tap the chevron to toggle a heading's subtree, or swipe left on a heading to cycle collapsed → children only → fully expanded.
- *Move*: drag the grip at the right of a heading to move it with its subtree (Settings → Quick Settings → *Drag handle on headings* moves it to the left or turns it off). The blue line snaps between two headings; moving sideways steps through the levels that fit, rightward being deeper, and a tag names the result (*into* a heading, *same level as* one, or *top level*). Letting go over the top bar or the mode line, or pressing Escape, cancels.
- *Complete or archive*: swipe right. A heading with an active TODO keyword jumps to the first DONE-type keyword. Otherwise it opens the Archive, Refile or Cancel prompt, and an archived heading unarchives directly.
- *Archive* (*Unarchive* for an archived heading) moves the subtree to its ~org-archive-location~ or back, from a panel that shows the destination first (see [[#archiving][Archiving]]). The ~:ARCHIVE:~ tag and ~ARCHIVE_*~ properties can be edited or removed in the general editor.
- *Moving in steps* (↑ ↓ ← →): ↑ and ↓ reorder a heading among its siblings with its subtree. ← promotes it one level, right after its former parent. → demotes it one level, as the last child of the heading before it. At a boundary a short status message says so.
- *The general editor* (📋 *Edit details*) is a popup with five tabs, so nothing is a long scroll: *Dates*, *Tags*, *Props*, *Files* and *More* (priority and tables). A tab you have edited shows a dot, and a note beside the buttons names them ("Changed: Dates, Tags"). Each tab shows how many items it holds.
  - *SCHEDULED, DEADLINE and a plain timestamp*: date and time pickers, a repeat selector (every N hours, days, weeks, months or years) and an optional warning delay (~-3d~ shows a deadline three days early). The three are independent, each with its own *Clear*. See [[#agenda][Agenda]] for how a plain timestamp differs (it doesn't carry forward, and lives in the title).
  - *Tags*: removable chips (tap to remove) and an input with an *Add* button (Enter also adds). Suggestions appear as you type: every tag used in the open document or a loaded agenda file (most used first) plus tags declared on a ~#+TAGS:~ line, narrowed to what you typed and excluding tags the heading already has. One tap adds one.
  - *Priority*: buttons A, B, C and None. Priorities outside A to C aren't reachable here.
  - *Properties*: an editable key/value row for each, with a remove button and an *Add property* row. The Key field completes from every key used in the open document or a loaded agenda file (most used first) plus ones the app reads or writes (~CUSTOM_ID~, ~EFFORT~, ~Effort_ALL~, ~ID~, the ~ARCHIVE_*~ set); other keys still work. A row with a blank key is dropped on commit. This is also how you set a ~CUSTOM_ID~ for ~[[#id]]~-style links (see [[#links-and-images][Links and images]]).

  Three buttons govern every tab: *Cancel* discards everything and closes, *Reset* restores every field to how it was when the editor opened, and *OK* commits every tab and closes. Nothing is written until *OK*. Above them are three immediate actions. *Add table* inserts a table into the body and closes the editor. *Delete table* removes the heading's most recently added table after a confirmation, and is disabled when there is none. *Attach* closes the editor and opens the attachment picker (see [[#attachments][Attachments]]). If any field has changed, these three first ask *Commit and continue*, *Discard and continue* or *Keep editing*; with no changes they act at once.

  Existing properties also show as a small read-only line under the heading while drawers are visible for it (~#+STARTUP: showeverything~, or manually cycled to fully expanded; see [[#folding-and-startup][Folding and #+STARTUP]]). Tapping it opens the action menu.

- *Block content* (~#+BEGIN_SRC~, ~#+BEGIN_QUOTE~, ~#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE~ and so on) is shown read-only, under the same drawer-visibility rule as properties. Folded, it shows a "collapsed block" label: tap it to reveal the content, and tap it again to re-fold. Edit blocks in [[#the-plain-text-editor][Text view]]. Any ~#+BEGIN_NAME~ and ~#+END_NAME~ pair works, and three names are displayed specially:
  - ~QUOTE~: inline markup is interpreted, and the block is indented on both margins with a left border.
  - ~VERSE~: inline markup is interpreted, and every source line stays its own line.
  - ~CENTER~: inline markup is interpreted, and its paragraphs are centered.

  Everything else (~SRC~, ~EXAMPLE~, ~COMMENT~, custom names) is shown literally.

  Export (see [[#export][Export]]) turns ~SRC~ into a code block with its language kept, ~QUOTE~ into a blockquote and drops ~COMMENT~. A ~SRC~ language is not syntax-highlighted in the outline, and only ~js~ blocks can run (see [[#source-blocks][Source blocks]]).

*** A heading's "text"
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: a-headings-text
:END:

Org has no separate description field: everything after a heading, up to the next heading, belongs to it, and can include several paragraphs, lists and tables in any order. *Edit text* opens all of it as one block of raw org syntax in a popup, like Settings' *Menu labels* editor (see [[#menu-customization][Menu customization]]): a large textarea with *Cancel* (discard and close), *Reset* (reload the original text and keep the popup open) and *OK* (save and close). The heading's rendered body is hidden from the outline while the popup is open. Typing ~- [ ]~ at the start of a line becomes a checklist item on save, as in the file.

-----

** Undo/redo and History
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: undoredo-and-history
:END:

Every edit can be undone and redone: text, TODO state, priority, tags, properties, moving, archiving, capturing, all of it. The command palette's *Undo history* opens a panel with *‹ Undo* and *Redo ›* buttons, a list of every step since the file was opened (current position marked) and a *diff* toggle on each entry showing what it changed.

Tap any entry to jump there. Entries past your position are dimmer. A new edit from an undone point discards what was ahead of it; browsing the list discards nothing.

A step is one completed edit action (saving a title, toggling a checkbox, archiving a heading), not a keystroke, and an edit that changes nothing adds none.

History is unlimited while a file stays open. It survives closing and reopening (the 200 most recent steps) only if the text on reopen matches what the app last had; if the file changed elsewhere, the old history is dropped. Undo and redo reapply the file's ~#+STARTUP~ visibility instead of keeping fold state.

Landing on a step identical to the last saved text clears the modified indicator.

*If the filename shows modified (red) and nothing you did explains it*, check the first history entry. If it reads "Opened (resumed unsaved local version)" instead of "Opened", the file had an unsaved edit from an earlier session, and reopening resumed it instead of starting from what is stored. Save to make that version the real one, or jump back in the history list if it wasn't what you wanted.

-----

** Lists, tables, and body text
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: lists-tables-and-body-text
:END:

- *Lists*: ordered, unordered, checkboxes, description lists (~term \:: description~) and nested sub-lists. Tap an item's text for edit, add-below and delete actions.
- *Checkboxes* cycle unchecked → in-progress → done. A progress cookie in a heading's title (~[3/8]~, ~[40%]~, or the blank ~[/]~) is recalculated whenever a checkbox in its subtree changes, counting its own list and every descendant heading's, as org does. A ~:COOKIE_DATA:~ property changes what is counted: ~checkbox~ or ~todo~ picks the kind when a heading has both, both words count both, and ~recursive~ with ~todo~ extends TODO counting to the whole subtree. Without it, only checkboxes are counted, recursively.
- *Tables*: tap a cell to edit it in place. The *⎌* button beside the field discards the edit and restores the cell's text (on a phone there is no Escape key). Row and column controls sit below the table, and ~#+TBLFM:~ formulas are evaluated (see [[#table-formulas][Table formulas]]). *Header rows* are the rows before the table's first horizontal rule (~|---+---|~) and show bold; a table with no rule has no header, and a later rule only separates groups.
- *Paragraphs*: tap the text for edit, add-below and delete actions.
- *Captions, names and image sizes*: ~#+CAPTION:~, ~#+NAME:~, ~#+ATTR_HTML:~ (or ~#+ATTR_ORG:~), ~#+HEADER:~ and ~#+RESULTS:~ lines directly above a paragraph, image, table or block describe it. A caption shows in italics with its markup rendered; ~#+ATTR_HTML: :width 300 :align center~ sizes and centers the images in that paragraph (a plain number is pixels; ~%~ and ~em~ work). The other lines stay visible as small muted text, exactly as written.

Undo/redo covers every edit (see [[#undoredo-and-history][Undo/redo and History]]).

*** Table formulas
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: table-formulas
:END:

~#+TBLFM:~ formulas use a subset of org's formula language. Org hands anything beyond simple arithmetic to Emacs Calc, which is not reproduced here.

| Name | What it does |
|---+---|
| ~+ - * /~ | Arithmetic. Division by zero gives ~#ERROR~ |
| ~^~ | Exponent, right-associative (~2^3^2~ is 512) |
| ~sqrt(x)~ | Square root; a negative input gives a complex number, ~sqrt(-4)~ is ~(0, 2)~ |
| ~floor(x)~, ~ceil(x)~, ~round(x)~, ~trunc(x)~ | Round toward −∞, toward +∞, to nearest (an exact .5 goes away from zero), toward zero. An optional second argument keeps that many decimals: ~round($1, 2)~ |
| ~sin(x)~, ~cos(x)~, ~tan(x)~ | Degrees by default (see the ~D~ and ~R~ flags) |
| ~arcsin(x)~, ~arccos(x)~, ~arctan(x)~ | Inverse trig, under Calc's names (not ~asin~); outside −1 to 1 the result is complex |
| ~ln(x)~, ~log10(x)~, ~log(x, base)~ | Logarithms; ~log(x)~ is natural. ~x~ of 0, or a ~base~ of exactly 1, gives ~#ERROR~; a negative number gives a complex result |
| ~exp(x)~, ~exp10(x)~ | e^x and 10^x |
| ~pi~, ~inf~ | Constants, written bare; ~-inf~ works |
| ~$name~ | A constant from a ~#+CONSTANTS:~ line |
| ~vsum~, ~vmean~, ~vcount~, ~vmin~, ~vmax~, ~vmedian~ (~range~) | Sum, mean, count of non-blank cells, minimum, maximum, median |
| ~vvar~, ~vpvar~, ~vsdev~, ~vpsdev~ (~range~) | Sample and population variance and standard deviation. As in Calc, there is no plain ~variance~ or ~stddev~ |
| ~if(c,t,f)~ | ~t~ if ~c~ is true (non-zero or non-empty), else ~f~; only the chosen branch is evaluated |
| ~and(a,b)~, ~or(a,b)~, ~not(a)~ | Function forms of the logical operators; they don't short-circuit |
| ~string(ref)~ | A cell's raw text as a string |
| ~"text"~ | A string literal (~\"~ for a quote inside it) |
| ~date(ref)~, ~date(Y,M,D)~, ~now()~ | Date values (see below) |
| ~deg(x)~ | Turns an HMS duration back into a plain number of days |
| ~date-to-time(ref)~ | A date value from a wider range of date strings |
| ~format-time-string(fmt, time, utc)~ | Formats a time with ~%~ codes (see [[#capture-templates][Capture templates]]) |
| ~uconv(value, "from", "to")~ | Unit conversion (see below) |

*Logic*: comparisons (~==~ or ~=~, ~!=~, ~<~, ~>~, ~<=~, ~>=~) give ~1~ or ~0~. They bind tighter than ~&&~ and ~||~, which bind looser than ~+ - * /~, so ~$1 >= 50 && $2 >= 50~ means ~($1 >= 50) && ($2 >= 50)~. ~!x~ is logical NOT. ~&&~, ~||~ and ~if~ short-circuit, so ~if($1 != 0, 100 / $1, 0)~ never divides by zero. Nested ~if~ calls make an else-if chain: ~if($1 >= 90, "A", if($1 >= 80, "B", "C"))~. A string literal is text and ~string(ref)~ reads a cell as text, so ~string($1) == "Sales"~ compares text, where a bare ~$1 == "Sales"~ would try to read the cell as a number.

*Named constants*: a ~#+CONSTANTS:~ line anywhere in the file defines constants, used as ~$name~: ~#+CONSTANTS: c=299792458 g=9.81~. Names are space-separated, several lines combine, and a later value wins. An undefined ~$name~ gives ~#ERROR~. There is no built-in physical-constants library (org's optional ~constants.el~); only ~pi~ and ~inf~ are built in.

*Dates and times*: a cell holding an org timestamp (~[YYYY-MM-DD]~ or ~<YYYY-MM-DD>~, with an optional time and day name) is read as a date as soon as it is referenced, so ~$3 = $1 - $2~ subtracts two timestamp cells. Every component is range-checked (month 1 to 12, a day within that month's length with leap years, hour 0 to 23, minute 0 to 59), so ~<2026-06-34>~ gives ~#ERROR~. ~date(ref)~ differs from a bare reference only for a cell that isn't a timestamp: bare, it reads as an ordinary number; wrapped, it gives ~#ERROR~, which is useful when a formula should fail loudly. ~date(Y, M, D)~ builds a date from three numbers (~date(2028, 2, 29)~ is valid, ~date(2026, 2, 29)~ is not).

- Subtracting two dates gives days as an integer, or, if either has a time of day, a duration in Calc's HMS form (~8@ 30' 0"~ for 8.5 hours).
- Adding or subtracting a number shifts a date by that many days and writes it back as a timestamp: ~date($1) + 14~ gives ~<2026-09-08>~.
- ~deg()~ turns an HMS duration back into days for further arithmetic: ~deg(date($2) - date($1)) * 24;%.2f~ gives ~8.50~ hours. ~now()~ is the current date and time.
- ~date-to-time(ref)~ accepts every timestamp ~date()~ does, plus ISO 8601 (~2026-01-15T10:30:00Z~), RFC 822 and US (~01/15/2026~) strings, parsed by the browser. An unparseable string gives ~#ERROR~.
- ~format-time-string(fmt, time, utc)~ uses the capture-template ~%~ codes: ~format-time-string("%Y-%m-%d", $1)~ gives ~2026-01-15~. ~time~ defaults to now and takes a date value or Unix seconds; a non-zero ~utc~ formats in UTC, otherwise the device's time zone is used.

*References*: ~$N~ is column N of the current row, ~@N$M~ is row N, column M, ~@-N~ and ~@+N~ are rows relative to the target, ~@<~, ~@>~, ~$<~ and ~$>~ are the first and last row or column, and a range such as ~$1..$3~ or ~@1$1..@3$2~ is an aggregate function's argument. A range may omit the column (~@2..@6~) to mean those rows in the formula's own column. Rows count every actual row, including the header; a horizontal rule has no row number. The column shorthand ~$M=~ (no ~@~, applied to every row) skips rows before the first horizontal rule, while an explicit ~@1$2=~ still changes that row. A table with no rule has no header, so nothing is skipped.

~@I~, ~@II~, ~@III~ refer to horizontal rules by repeated "I" characters, not Roman numerals (~@IIII~ is the fourth). An offset such as ~@III+2~ is the data row that many rows after (or, with ~-~, before) the rule. A range between two rules, ~vsum(@I..@II)~, covers the data rows strictly between them. A count past the last rule clamps to the end of the table.

*Targets*: a formula's target is one cell (~@N$M=~), a range (~@N$M..@N$M=~, applied to each cell; each end needs an explicit row) or a whole column (~$M=~). Several formulas in one ~#+TBLFM:~ line are separated by ~::~ and run in order, each seeing the earlier results. Only the first ~#+TBLFM:~ line directly below a table counts.

*Recalculating* is explicit. A *🔢 Calc* button below a table with a ~#+TBLFM:~ line recalculates that table. *Recalculate all tables* in the command palette (~org-table-recalculate-buffer-tables~, also usable in an Extras entry) recalculates every table as one undo step. A malformed formula is reported, and only its own table is skipped.

*Blank and non-numeric cells*: by default a blank cell in a direct reference (~$1+$2~) reads as 0 but is left out of a range, so ~vmean~ averages only the non-blank cells and ~vcount~ skips it. Text that isn't a number reads as ~nan~ and propagates, so a stray label shows a problem instead of a plausible wrong number (the ~N~ flag below reads it as 0).

*Mode flags*: a trailing ~;flags~ string after the expression:

| Flag | Effect |
|---+---|
| ~%.Nf~, ~fN~ | Fixed, N decimals (~%0.Nf~ also works): ~4.85;f2~ gives ~4.85~ |
| ~%d~ | Truncates toward zero: ~4.85~ gives ~4~ |
| ~nN~ | Normal notation, N significant figures: ~3.14159265;n5~ gives ~3.1416~ |
| ~sN~ | Scientific notation, N figures: ~123456.789;s3~ gives ~1.23e5~ |
| ~eN~ | Engineering notation (exponent a multiple of 3): ~123456.789;e3~ gives ~123e3~ |
| ~pN~ | Computes at N significant digits, in arbitrary precision (see [[#development][Development]]). Degree-mode trig is limited to about double precision, and sqrt of a negative still errors |
| ~E~ | Keeps a blank cell in a range (as ~nan~) and reads a blank direct reference as ~nan~ |
| ~N~ | Non-numeric text (with ~E~, blanks too) reads as 0 instead of ~nan~ |
| ~D~, ~R~ | Angle mode for the trig functions: degrees or radians. Degrees is the default, so ~D~ changes nothing |
| ~T~, ~U~, ~t~ | Duration mode. Cells matching ~HH:MM[:SS]~ (or a bare integer, in seconds) are read as durations, and the result is ~HH:MM:SS~ (~T~), ~HH:MM~ (~U~) or decimal hours to two places (~t~). Without a flag, ~HH:MM~ text isn't a duration. Negative durations work, and ~org-table-duration-hour-zero-padding~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]], default on) pads the hours |
| ~F~ | Fraction mode: exact rational results (~1/3;F~ is exactly ~1/3~, and ~$1/$2;F~ on 3 and 6 is ~1/2~; a whole result shows without ~/1~). A function with a rational result stays exact (~sqrt(4);F~ is ~2~); otherwise a short approximation (denominator under 1,000,000) is shown |
| ~FS~ | Fraction mode as a mixed number: ~14/4;FS~ is ~3 + 1/2~. ~S~ alone does nothing, since general Symbolic mode isn't implemented |

An unrecognized flag is ignored. Examples:

#+begin_example
|  Task 1 |   Task 2 |    Total |
|---------+----------+----------|
|    2:12 |     1:47 | 03:59:00 |
|    2:12 |     1:47 |    03:59 |
| 3:02:20 | -2:07:00 |     0.92 |
#+TBLFM: @2$3=$1+$2;T::@3$3=$1+$2;U::@4$3=$1+$2;t
#+end_example

#+begin_example
| Top | Bottom | Fraction | Mixed number |
|-----+--------+----------+--------------|
|   3 |      6 | 1/2      | 1/2          |
|  12 |      9 | 4/3      | 1 + 1/3      |
|  14 |      4 | 7/2      | 3 + 1/2      |
#+TBLFM: $3=$1/$2;F::$4=$1/$2;FS
#+end_example

*Errors*: a formula that fails when evaluated (an out-of-range reference, a range where one value is expected) writes ~#ERROR~ into that one cell, and the rest of the table still updates. A formula that can't be parsed (bad syntax, an unknown function) is reported for the whole recalculation.

*Raw Elisp*: a formula starting with a quote, like org's ~'(function-name arg ...)~, bypasses the grammar above. One function is supported, ~orgtbl-ascii-draw(value, min, max, width)~, which draws a bar in the cell using org's 11-character gradient. A ~value~ outside ~[min, max]~ shows ~too small~ or ~too large~, and ~width~ defaults to 12. Each argument may be a number, a ~$N~ reference or a parenthesized expression such as ~($2 * 2)~.

*Unit conversion*: ~uconv(value, "from", "to")~, such as ~uconv($1, "mi/hr", "m/s")~, uses the mathjs unit library (see Development). It handles compound units (~kg/m^3~) and converts temperature as an absolute reading (~0 degC~ is ~32 degF~, like Calc's ~u t~ command rather than the relative change of ~u c~). Unlike Calc's two-argument form, the source unit is explicit. An incompatible pair (~m~ to ~kg~) or an unknown unit gives ~#ERROR~. Common units: length (~m~, ~ft~, ~km~, ~mi~, ~in~, ~cm~), mass (~kg~, ~lb~, ~g~, ~oz~), temperature (~degC~, ~degF~, ~K~), volume (~L~, ~gal~, ~mL~), time (~s~, ~min~, ~hr~, ~day~), speed (~mi/hr~, ~m/s~), data (~MB~, ~GB~), pressure (~bar~, ~psi~, ~atm~), energy (~J~, ~kWh~) and area (~m^2~, ~acre~). Names mostly match Calc's; ~tsp~ and ~tbsp~ are aliases for mathjs's ~teaspoon~ and ~tablespoon~. The full list is at https://mathjs.org/docs/datatypes/units.html.

*Complex numbers*: ~(re, im)~ or ~(r; θ)~ in a cell or formula, and ~i~ for (0, 1). ~+ - * / ^~, ~sqrt~, ~exp~, ~ln~, ~log10~, the trig functions and ~vsum~, ~vmean~, ~vprod~ accept them, along with ~re~, ~im~, ~conj~, ~abs~, ~arg~, ~polar~ and ~rect~. Whole numbers stay exact and other parts show as floats (~2.~), a zero imaginary part drops to a plain number, and ~pN~ sets the working digits. Unlike Calc, ~i~ is the number, so ~2+3*i~ is ~(2, 3)~, not ~3 i + 2~.

#+begin_example
| (1, 2) | (3, 4) | (-5, 10) |
#+TBLFM: $3=$1*$2
#+end_example

*Vectors and matrices*: ~[1, 2, 3]~ and ~[[1, 2], [3, 4]]~ in a cell or formula; a cell range such as ~$1..$3~ is a vector of its non-blank cells. ~+ -~ and ~* /~ by a number work elementwise; ~*~ is a dot product for two vectors, a matrix product for matrices, and ~^~ takes a matrix to an integer power. Functions: ~det~, ~inv~, ~trn~, ~tr~, ~cross~, ~vlen~, ~abs~ (the length), and the ~v~ aggregates, which flatten.

Out of scope: Emacs Calc beyond the above (symbolic algebra, the rest of Calc's vector and matrix library), named-field references, and recalculation on every keystroke.

*** Plots
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: plots
:END:

A ~#+PLOT:~ line directly above a table (several stacked lines combine their options) graphs the table's data. A *📊 Plot* button below the table, beside *🔢 Calc* when present, shows the graph inline, and tapping it again hides it. This is a subset of org-plot: it reads org-plot's own ~#+PLOT:~ options, so an unmodified line works, but it renders inline SVG instead of calling gnuplot.

~type:2d~ (the default) and ~type:radar~ are supported; ~type:3d~ and ~type:grid~ are refused with an error. For 2d, ~with:~ picks ~lines~ (the default), ~points~, ~boxes~ (~histograms~ renders the same) or ~impulses~.

| Option | Meaning |
|---+---|
| ~title~ | A quoted string |
| ~ind~ | The 1-based column giving the x position (2d) or the axis label (radar); default 1 |
| ~deps~ | A parenthesized list of 1-based columns to plot; default every column except ~ind~ |
| ~labels~ | A parenthesized list of quoted series names; default the header row |
| ~transpose~, ~trans~ | ~yes~, ~y~ or ~t~ swaps rows and columns first, which is how a radar chart gets its axes from columns |
| ~min~, ~max~ | The y range (2d), or the shared range of every radar axis |
| ~xmin~, ~xmax~ | The x range (2d, when ~ind~ is numeric) |
| ~ticks~ | The number of y gridlines; default 5 |

org-plot's gnuplot scripting options (~set~, ~line~, ~script~, ~file~, ~map~, ~timefmt~) are accepted but have no effect, so a copied line never errors.

The graph is cached per ~#+PLOT:~ line and table data, and editing the table re-renders it the next time it is shown. Collapsing the heading hides it, and the *Plot* button needs a fresh tap after expanding.

-----

** Inline text markup
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: inline-text-markup
:END:

All six of org's emphasis markers work in headings, paragraphs and list items:

| Markup | Syntax | Renders as |
|---+---+---|
| Bold | ~*bold text*~ | *bold text* |
| Italic | ~/italic text/~ | /italic text/ |
| Underline | ~_underline text_~ | underlined |
| Strikethrough | ~+strikethrough text+~ | +strikethrough text+ |
| Verbatim | ~=verbatim text=~ | ~verbatim text~ (literal, not further parsed) |
| Code | =~code text~= | ~code text~ (literal, not further parsed) |

A marker opens after the start of a line, whitespace or one of ~-({'"~, and isn't followed by whitespace. It closes where it isn't preceded by whitespace and is followed by the end of the line, whitespace or closing punctuation. Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough nest (~*bold /italic/ bold*~); verbatim and code never do.

*Horizontal rule*: a line of only dashes, at least five (~-----~), is a horizontal rule. Whitespace around the dashes is fine; any other character on the line makes it a paragraph.

*Hard line break*: a line ending in two backslashes (~\\~) forces a line break, in paragraphs, QUOTE and CENTER blocks and every export format. Otherwise the source lines of a paragraph or list item reflow together with a space, as in org.

*Subscript and superscript*: ~x_i~ and ~x^2~ work without braces, and braces (~x_{alpha}~, ~10^{100}~) are always accepted. ~org-use-sub-superscripts~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]) controls them in the outline and in every export except ASCII (which prints ~_x~ either way); a file's ~#+OPTIONS: ^:~ wins:

| Value | Behavior |
|---+---|
| ~t~ (default) | Both ~x_i~ and ~x_{i}~ are interpreted |
| ~{}~ | Only the braced form ~x_{i}~ is interpreted; a bare ~x_i~ stays literal text |
| ~nil~ | Disabled entirely; ~_~ / ~^~ are always literal characters |

~_~ also marks underline: underline needs whitespace, a line start or punctuation before it (~_underlined_~), subscript a non-space character (~a_b~). Script content is literal, so ~x_{*bold*}~ doesn't interpret the ~*bold*~.

*Footnotes*: ~[fn:label]~ is a reference, shown as a small tappable superscript that jumps to the definition, even under a folded heading. A definition can be inline, ~[fn:label:the note text]~, anonymous, ~[fn::an anonymous note]~, or a separate line starting ~[fn:label]~ (like ~[fn:1] The actual definition.~). Markdown export uses GFM's ~[^label]~, HTML a jump-linked superscript with a back-linked Footnotes section.

Table cells render inline markup too; tap one to edit its raw text and tap away to commit.

*** Footnote commands
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: footnotes
:END:

In the outline, open a paragraph, a list item or a heading's text with *Edit text*, put the cursor after the words the note belongs to and tap *Footnote*. A sheet (a dialog on a large screen) asks for the label, already the next free number, and the note, with a switch to write it inline; *Insert* adds the reference and the note under ~* Footnotes~, and Undo takes it back. Tap a reference to see its note and *Edit note*, *Go to the note* or *Delete footnote*; a reference with no note offers *Create the note*. With a paragraph selected from the keyboard, the *Footnote* command opens that paragraph's sheet.

In Text view, *Footnote* (~org-footnote-action~, ~C-c C-x f~, palette) does the right thing at the cursor: on a reference it jumps to the definition (offering to create one if there is none), on a definition's label it jumps back to the reference, and anywhere else it adds a new footnote. Where a footnote can't go (start of a line, source blocks, comments, links, inside another reference) it offers the one-key menu: ~s~ort, ~r~enumber, ~S~ both, ~n~ormalize, ~d~elete.

- *Insert footnote* (~org-footnote-new~): a reference at the cursor and the start of its definition under ~* Footnotes~ at the end of the file, with the cursor there to write it. The label is the next unused number; an existing label adds another reference to it, and an empty one makes an anonymous ~[fn::]~.
- *Normalize footnotes* (~org-footnote-normalize~): every footnote becomes a numbered one in reading order, inline and anonymous notes become definitions, and all definitions move under ~* Footnotes~ (~DEFINITION NOT FOUND.~ for a reference nobody defined).
- *Sort footnotes* (~org-footnote-sort~) puts the definitions in the order of their references. *Renumber footnotes* (~org-footnote-renumber-fn:N~) numbers ~fn:1~, ~fn:2~… by first reference.
- *Delete footnote* (~org-footnote-delete~): the one at the cursor, or the label you give, with every definition and reference.

Insert, sort, renumber, normalize and delete work from any view, and Undo reverses them. Settings: ~org-footnote-section~ (the heading; ~nil~ keeps each definition at the end of its own section), ~org-footnote-auto-label~, ~org-footnote-define-inline~ and ~org-footnote-auto-adjust~ (renumber and/or sort after adding or deleting). ~#+STARTUP:~ accepts ~fninline~, ~fnlocal~, ~fnauto~, ~fnprompt~, ~fnconfirm~, ~fnplain~, ~fnadjust~ and ~nofnadjust~.

*** LaTeX math fragments
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: latex-fragments
:END:

Math in a heading, paragraph or list item renders as typeset math with [[https://katex.org][KaTeX]], vendored locally (no CDN). It is display-only: the ~.org~ file's text is untouched, and editing shows the raw source.

| Delimiter | Kind | Restrictions |
|---+---+---|
| ~\(...\)~ | Inline | None — org's own recommended form |
| ~\[...\]~ | Display | None |
| ~$$...$$~ | Display | None |
| ~$...$~ | Inline | No whitespace directly inside the delimiters; the closing ~$~ must be followed by whitespace or punctuation, but never a dash (avoiding ~$5-10~ reading as math) |
| ~\begin{env}...\end{env}~ | Display | ~\begin~ must start a line, preceded by nothing but whitespace |

~$...$~ avoids misreading currency: ~costs $5 and $10 total~ stays text. The first content character can't be whitespace, comma, semicolon or period, the character before the closing ~$~ can't be whitespace, comma or period, and it needs two characters of content (use ~\(x\)~ for one).

~\(...\)~, ~\[...\]~, ~$$...$$~ and ~\begin{env}...\end{env}~ can span lines, even across a blank line; ~$...$~ allows at most two newlines. KaTeX doesn't treat ~%~ as a comment. A fragment KaTeX can't render shows its raw source with a dashed border. KaTeX supports a large subset of LaTeX, not all of it.

Math renders wherever inline markup does: the outline, the read-only Docs viewer and HTML export (KaTeX's CSS is added only when the export has math). LaTeX export writes it unchanged; Markdown, ASCII and ODT export pass the raw source through as text.

*Examples*: the source ~The quadratic formula is \(x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}\).~ renders inline with a proper fraction bar and a square-root radical. This ~align~ environment:

#+BEGIN_SRC
\begin{align}
E &= mc^2 \\
F &= ma \\
a^2 + b^2 &= c^2
\end{align}
#+END_SRC

renders three right-aligned equations, lined up at the ~&~ marks and automatically numbered (1) to (3), which is KaTeX's own behavior for ~align~. The ~\\~ ending a line there ends an equation; it is unrelated to org's hard line break above.

-----

** Searching
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: searching
:END:

Open the command palette's *Search* (or god-mode's ~s~, see [[#keybindings][Keybindings]]) to search the open document, case-insensitively: headings, tags, TODO keyword, priority, properties (key or value), SCHEDULED and DEADLINE timestamps, paragraphs, list items, table cells and block content. When any are configured it also searches every file in ~org-agenda-files~.

Results appear at once from what is loaded and fill in as each agenda file finishes (a file that fails to fetch is left out). The query box and its options live in the minibuffer (see [[#modeline][Modeline and minibuffer]]). Results update as you type, grouped under their heading with the match highlighted; a result from another file shows its name.

Search covers the whole document whatever the fold state. Tapping a result expands what is needed to reveal it, scrolls to it with a brief highlight and switches to its file first if needed.

*** Filter tokens

Tokens in the query box combine as an implicit AND:

- ~word~ or ~+word~: the entry (title, tags, TODO state, priority, properties, planning and body text) must contain it. ~-word~ excludes entries that contain it. ~+computer +wifi -ethernet~, or just ~computer wifi -ethernet~, finds entries with "computer" and "wifi" but not "ethernet", as in org's ~org-search-view~. So a query like ~-5~ means "exclude entries containing 5", not the literal text; use Regex mode for that.
- ~tag:urgent~: the heading must have this tag, inherited tags included. ~-tag:urgent~ excludes it.
- ~todo:KEYWORD~: the TODO state must equal this (case-insensitive), as in ~todo:WAITING~. ~-todo:KEYWORD~ excludes it; a heading with no keyword passes an exclude.
- ~priority:X~: the priority must equal this, as in ~priority:A~. ~-priority:X~ excludes it.
- ~key:value~: any other ~key:value~ matches a property ~key~ whose value contains ~value~ (substring, case-insensitive), such as ~spouse:Mary~. ~-key:value~ excludes it.
- ~|~ inside ~tag:~, ~todo:~, ~priority:~ or ~key:value~ means "any of these": ~tag:urgent|blocked~, ~todo:TODO|WAITING~, ~assignee:Bob|Alice~. Negated, it means "none of these". It combines alternatives only within one filter. There is no OR between filters and no grouping; Match mode has both.

A word starting with ~+~ or ~-~ (a negative number, a hyphenated word) or shaped ~word:word~ (such as ~mailto:~) can be read as a filter; ~http://~ and ~https://~ URLs are not. Tag inheritance is on by default and property inheritance off, as in org. A query with only filters (~tag:work -someday~) returns the matching headings directly.

Example: ~+work todo:WAITING budget~ finds entries tagged ~work~, in WAITING state, containing "budget".

*** Regex mode

The *Regex* toggle in the minibuffer switches from plain substring matching to a regular expression, case-insensitive either way, in Emacs's syntax rather than JavaScript's. The biggest difference: an unescaped ~(~, ~)~, ~{~, ~}~ or ~|~ is literal, and grouping needs ~\(~ and ~\)~, alternation ~\|~, and an interval ~\{n,m\}~. With Regex off, a ~.~ or ~(~ in the query simply matches that character.

Supported: backreferences (~\1~ to ~\9~), word and symbol boundaries (~\<~, ~\>~, ~\_<~, ~\_>~, ~\b~, ~\B~), POSIX classes in brackets (~[[:digit:]]~, ~[[:alpha:]]~) and whole-string anchors (~\`~ and ~\'~, distinct from the line anchors ~^~ and ~$~). Constructs that depend on a buffer's syntax table (~\s<~, ~\s>~, ~\sc~, ~\S-~ and similar) aren't supported and show an error naming the construct. An invalid pattern shows a clear error, so it is never mistaken for "no matches".

Example: ~^\(Buy\|Fix\)~ finds headings whose title starts with "Buy" or "Fix".

*** Match mode

*Match*, beside *Regex* in the options popover (the ~⋯~ button at the search bar's right edge, which shows a check mark by the active one and a dot when either is on), uses org's tag and property match grammar, the one behind ~C-c / m~. Match and Regex are mutually exclusive.

~|~ is the lowest-precedence operator and splits the query into OR'd groups. Within a group, ~+family~ (or a bare ~family~) and ~-work~ combine as AND, so ~family+work|urgent~ means "(family AND work) OR urgent". A condition can also compare a property, ~PROPERTY="value"~ with ~=~, ~<>~, ~<~, ~>~, ~<=~ or ~>=~, combined freely with tags (~work+PRIORITY_TEST="B"~). ~TODO~, ~LEVEL~, ~PRIORITY~ and ~CATEGORY~ work as pseudo-properties, as in org. An empty query, an empty group beside a stray ~|~, or an unparseable condition gives a clear error. Replace is disabled in this mode.

Example: ~work+urgent|blocked~ finds headings tagged both ~work~ and ~urgent~, or tagged ~blocked~.

*** Search extra files
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: search-extra-files
:END:

~org-agenda-text-search-extra-files~ lists more files to search, in addition to the file you have open and your [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]]. It is the same ~scheme:path~ syntax (~github:~, ~webdav:~, ~local:~), semicolon-separated:

#+BEGIN_EXAMPLE
org-agenda-text-search-extra-files: github:notes/reference.org;webdav:archive/2024.org
#+END_EXAMPLE

Set it in *Settings → Quick Settings → Search extra files*, or per document in Local Variables. The files are searched, and nothing else: they don't appear in the Agenda, TODO or tag views, which makes this the place for notes that should be findable but not scheduled. A file listed here and as an agenda file is searched once. Tapping a result opens its file. A file that is still loading, or can't be loaded, is named above the results, so it never just quietly finds nothing. *Replace* works on the open file and your agenda files only.

*** Search and replace

The options button (~⋯~) also shows *Replace*, which starts an Emacs-style ~query-replace~ (or ~query-replace-regexp~, following the Regex toggle) with the search text as the pattern. It walks every [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]] file that has a match, starting with the open one, and a file it enters opens as its own tab. It asks for the replacement text, then offers each match:

| Key | Action |
|---+---|
| ~y~ or Space | Replace this one and go on |
| ~n~ or Delete | Skip it |
| ~q~ or Return | Stop the walk (replacements already made stay; the rest is untouched) |
| ~.~ | Replace this one and stop |
| ~!~ | Replace all remaining matches in the current file, then go on to the next file with a match |

Buttons for all five sit beside the prompt for devices without a keyboard. ~$1~ to ~$9~ in the replacement text are filled from the match's capture groups. As in Emacs, nothing is saved automatically: each touched file is changed but unsaved, shown by its tab's modified indicator. A configured agenda file that can't be reached (a local file not already open) is left out; only open files and GitHub or WebDAV files can be walked.

Replace works on heading titles, paragraphs, list items and table cells. Tags, TODO state, priority, properties, planning timestamps and block content (~#+BEGIN_VERSE~, ~#+BEGIN_QUOTE~ and the like) are never replaced, because that could corrupt the document's syntax. Search still finds text inside blocks, and when all of a query's matches are inside block content, Replace says so ("N matches found only inside block content... not editable here; use Text view instead"). [[#the-plain-text-editor][Text view]]'s own search and replace has no such restriction and stays within that one document.

*** Narrow

When at least one match is in the open document, the results show *Narrow* with a count of those matches (cross-file results aren't counted). It works with any search mode. Tapping it restricts the outline to the matching headings plus their ancestors, so each match keeps its context, and a banner shows the count with a *Widen* button. It composes with [[#narrowing][subtree narrowing]]: narrow to a subtree, then to matches within it. Like subtree narrowing it survives a reload, and a heading renamed or removed in the meantime simply drops out.

Org's search is several tools (sparse trees, a match grammar, ~org-search-view~); here one box covers them, with Match mode for the fuller boolean grammar. Not included: sparse-tree refolding (Narrow is the nearest equivalent).

-----

** Modeline and minibuffer
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: modeline
:END:

A fixed two-row bar at the bottom of the screen, laid out like Emacs's frame: a dense modeline above a minibuffer.

*The modeline* is read-only, monospace and terse:

- *Modified indicator*: ~--~ unmodified, ~**~ modified, ~%%~ read-only, ~%*~ read-only and modified, Emacs's four states. Emacs's coding-system and line-ending segment is omitted, since the app always writes UTF-8 with Unix line endings.
- *Buffer name*: the document's name plus a suffix, ~(GitHub)~, ~(WebDAV)~, ~(Local)~ or ~(Imported)~.
- *Position*: ~Top~, ~Bot~, ~All~ or a percentage for how far down the visible area is, plus ~L~ and the line number when a heading is focused, and ~C~ and the column only while a text field is being edited. The app has no persistent cursor between edits, so otherwise there is no real column to show.
- *Date and time*, when ~display-time-mode~ is on (the default): formatted by ~display-time-format~ (default ~"%H:%M"~), using the same ~%<FORMAT>~ subset as [[#capture-templates][Capture templates]]. It updates at least every 30 seconds.
- *Clock*, when a clock is running anywhere in the document: the elapsed time of this clock-in in brackets, then the heading's title, like ~[⏱ 0:35] Write the quarterly report~. It shows the current session, not the task's lifetime total.

*The minibuffer*, below it, is the one strip for the status line, god-mode's chord echo and the search box (see [[#searching][Searching]]). Only one shows at a time: the search box while search is open, then the god-mode echo while a chord is in progress or has just completed (the chord and its command's name; see [[#god-mode][God-mode]]), and otherwise the last status message. A status message clears at your next keypress or tap, as Emacs's echo area clears at each new command.

Two variables control it, set in Global or Local Variables or in Settings → Quick Settings → *Modeline*:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---+---+---|
| ~display-time-mode~ | ~1~ (on) | Emacs's minor-mode toggle, with its ~1~ and ~0~ convention instead of ~t~ and ~nil~. ~0~ hides the date and time. |
| ~display-time-format~ | ~"%H:%M"~ | Emacs's variable and default. Any ~%<FORMAT>~ token that [[#capture-templates][Capture templates]] support works. |

-----

** Links and images
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: links-and-images
:END:

- ~[[target][description]]~ links render as tappable text.
- *Bare URLs* link too, typed in a sentence or wrapped as ~<https://example.com>~. The schemes are ~http~, ~https~, ~ftp~, ~mailto~, ~doi~, ~file~, ~github~, ~webdav~ and ~local~, so ~10:30~ or ~3:4~ is never a link. Trailing punctuation is left out (~see https://example.com/page.~ links the URL without the period); wrap the URL in ~<...>~ or ~[[...]]~ if it must end in one. ~doi:10.1145/1327452.1327492~ opens ~https://doi.org/...~.
- *Internal links* go to a heading by title (~[[*Some Heading]]~), by ~CUSTOM_ID~ (~[[#my-id]]~) or by a title search for bare text, expanding the ancestors and scrolling to the target. Set a ~CUSTOM_ID~ in the general editor (see [[#editing-your-outline][Editing your outline]]).
- *ID links*: ~[[id:3f2a-…][Meeting notes]]~ go to the heading with that ~:ID:~ property wherever it now lives. Tapping one looks in the open file, the other open tabs, your [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]], then files you have opened or saved here before (a remembered table, like ~org-id-locations~); the ⏎ button comes back. If nothing has the ID the status line says so, and if several headings share it the first is used. *Copy link to heading* (~org-store-link~, ~C-c l~) puts ~[[id:…][Title]]~ on the clipboard, adding an ~:ID:~ first if needed; *Add ID to heading* (~org-id-get-create~) only adds it; *Find links to this heading* searches this file and your Agenda Files.
- *Targets*: ~<<name>>~ is a spot a link can go to. The same words in triple angle brackets, ~<<<name>>>~, make a *radio target*: every plain use of those words in the file (any case, whole words) becomes a link to it. Code blocks are not read. HTML and LaTeX export turn targets into anchors and links.
- *The ⏎ button*: after you follow a link, a floating ⏎ at bottom-left goes back, one hop at a time, so a document with a table of contents is navigable on a touch device without a browser Back. It disappears when there is nowhere left to go.
- *Image links*: ~http://~ and ~https://~ image links render inline when ~#+STARTUP: inlineimages~ is set (off by default).
- *Local and relative image paths* on GitHub and WebDAV render too (~[[photo.png]]~, ~[[images/photo.png]]~, ~[[file:photo.png]]~, ~[[github:images/photo.png]]~), relative to the document's path, under the same ~#+STARTUP: inlineimages~ switch. Local files (File System Access) and iOS imports show an ~[image: path]~ placeholder, because reading a sibling file needs browser permission that can't be granted mid-render.
- *~file:~, ~github:~, ~webdav:~ and ~local:~ links* use org's ~::~ convention: an absolute path (~file:/home/user/notes.org~), a relative one (~file:projects/todo.org~), a headline (=file:~/notes.org::*Project Alpha=) or a text search (=file:~/notes.org::exact phrase=). Tapping one opens the document, as File → Open does, and jumps to the headline or match. A path with no scheme uses the backend the current document came from; an explicit scheme always uses that backend (~local:~ is a file on this device: see [[#android-app][Android app]]).

  The back button returns across documents to the heading the link was in, found by its title path (or the remembered scroll position if the heading was renamed or the link was in the preamble). This works only when both documents are on GitHub or WebDAV: a local file or iOS import can't be reopened from a link tap, because the browser needs a file-picker gesture for each file, so a message says so.
- *~attachment:~ links* are org-attach's link type, produced by *Attach* (see [[#attachments][Attachments]]). They are bracketed only (~[[attachment:photo.jpg]]~); a bare ~attachment:photo.jpg~ in text is not a link.

-----

** Configuration
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: configuration
:END:

Three layers set variables (Emacs Lisp variables or org directives), in org's own precedence: *Local Variables beats #+STARTUP beats Global Variables*. A variable left unset falls through to the next layer down.

1. *Global Variables* ([[#global-variables][below]]): an app-wide baseline, set in Settings.
2. *~#+STARTUP:~* ([[#folding-and-startup][below]]): a file's own directive. Only three variables have a ~#+STARTUP:~ shorthand, as in real org:

| Variable | ~#+STARTUP:~ keyword(s) |
|---+---|
| ~org-log-done~ | ~logdone~ (→ ~time~), ~lognotedone~ (→ ~note~) |
| ~org-startup-folded~ | ~overview~, ~content~, ~showall~, ~showeverything~, ~show2levels~, ~show3levels~, ~show4levels~, ~show5levels~ |
| ~org-startup-with-inline-images~ | ~inlineimages~ (→ ~t~), ~noinlineimages~ (→ ~nil~) |

3. *Local Variables* ([[#local-variables][below]]): a file's own ~# Local Variables:~ block, a general Emacs mechanism processed last.

-----

*** Global Variables
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: global-variables
:END:

Set in *Settings → Global Variables*. This is the lowest layer, and the only one not stored in a ~.org~ file. The format is one ~name: value~ per line, like a [[#local-variables][Local Variables]] block without its wrapper:

#+BEGIN_SRC
org-log-done: 'time
org-agenda-start-on-weekday: 1
#+END_SRC

Every Local Variables variable works here too, at app-wide precedence. Changes take effect on *Save*, with no reload, and they are part of *Export Settings* and *Import Settings…* (see [[#file-management][File management]]).

*Smart quotes are normalized*: iOS and many Android keyboards turn a typed straight quote into a curly one, but quoted values here (~org-xx-extra-menu~, ~org-xx-menu-aliases~, the [[#capture-templates][Capture Templates]] JSON) need straight quotes. Quick Settings, this text box and Capture Templates convert them back on save; quotes in ordinary prose are untouched.

-----

*** Folding and ~#+STARTUP~
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: folding-and-startup
:END:

org-pwa applies ~#+STARTUP:~ directives, typically on the first line. They can share a line or be spread across several, and the last matching keyword wins.

| Category | Keywords | Default |
|---+---+---|
| Heading visibility | ~overview~, ~content~, ~showall~, ~showeverything~, ~show2levels~, ~show3levels~, ~show4levels~, ~show5levels~ | ~showeverything~ |
| Inline images | ~inlineimages~, ~noinlineimages~ | ~noinlineimages~ |
| Progress logging on DONE | ~logdone~, ~lognotedone~ | neither (no logging) |

- ~overview~: only top-level headings, everything else folded.
- ~show2levels~ to ~show5levels~: like ~overview~ with that cutoff depth. Headings are shown through that level with no body text at any visible level, and deeper levels are folded.
- ~content~: every heading line shown, but body text (paragraphs, lists, tables) and properties hidden until you open a heading.
- ~showall~: body text, lists and tables shown. Property drawers (~:PROPERTIES:~) and blocks (~#+BEGIN_SRC~, ~#+BEGIN_QUOTE~ and the like) stay folded, one line each.
- ~showeverything~: ~showall~ plus drawers and blocks fully expanded.
- ~logdone~, ~lognotedone~: set ~org-log-done~ to ~time~ or ~note~ (see [[#progress-logging][Progress logging]]).

Cycling a heading to fully expanded always reveals its properties and blocks, whatever ~#+STARTUP:~ says, and collapsing hides them again. With no ~#+STARTUP~ line everything is shown, as in org.

-----

*** Local Variables
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: local-variables
:END:

Two forms, both general Emacs mechanisms: a first-line ~-*- var: val; -*-~ cookie, and a ~# Local Variables: ... # End:~ block, conventionally at the end of the file. Both can appear in one file, and the block wins a conflict. Most variables below also have a labeled control in Settings → *Quick Settings* (see [[#settings][Settings]]) for the app-wide baseline.

#+BEGIN_SRC
# -*- buffer-read-only: t; -*-
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC
# Local Variables:
# org-agenda-start-on-weekday: 1
# org-cycle-open-archived-trees: nil
# org-agenda-skip-comment-trees: t
# org-agenda-skip-archived-trees: t
# End:
#+END_SRC

The recognized variables, alphabetically. Those marked "(own)" are this app's extensions, not real org variables. Booleans are Lisp ~t~ or ~nil~, not JavaScript truthiness: the string ~"true"~ is not ~t~.

| Variable | Default | What it does |
|---+---+---|
| ~buffer-read-only~ | ~nil~ | Whether the buffer is read-only (see [[#keybindings][Keybindings]]: ~C-x C-q~, or *Toggle read-only* in the command palette) |
| ~calendar-date-style~ | ~american~ | Order of the date in ~diary-anniversary~, ~diary-cyclic~, ~diary-block~ and ~diary-date~: ~american~ (month day year), ~european~ (day month year) or ~iso~ (year month day) |
| ~calendar-latitude~ | ~35.994~ | Latitude for the solar forms and ~org-weather~ (Durham, NC) |
| ~calendar-longitude~ | ~-78.8986~ | Longitude for the same (Durham, NC) |
| ~org-agenda-category-filter-preset~ | unset | Agenda and TODO category chip to start with: a list like ~("+Work" "-Home")~. A ~-~ hides that category; several ~+~ keep any of them |
| ~org-agenda-effort-filter-preset~ | unset | Effort filter to start with, such as ~("+<2:00")~ (at most 2 hours; ~>~ is at least, ~=~ exactly) |
| ~org-agenda-files~ | unset (current file only) | Semicolon-separated ~scheme:path~ entries: more files for the Agenda and TODO views (see [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]]) |
| ~org-agenda-max-effort~ | ~nil~ | Per-day effort limit the ⏱ panel starts with: minutes, such as ~240~, or ~((agenda . 240) (todo . 120))~ |
| ~org-agenda-prefix-format~ | unset | Text before each row, such as ~"  %-12:c%?-12t% s"~, or an alist by view, ~((agenda . "…") (todo . "…"))~: ~%c~ category, ~%t~ time, ~%s~ Scheduled:/Deadline:, ~%e~ effort; ~%-12c~ pads right, ~%12c~ left, ~%?~ leaves the part out when empty. Unset keeps the usual row |
| ~org-agenda-regexp-filter-preset~ | unset | Search chip to start with: ~("+rent" "-later")~; Emacs regular expressions; every ~+~ pattern must match, no ~-~ pattern may |
| ~org-agenda-remove-times-when-in-prefix~ | ~t~ | Leave timestamps out of a heading's title in the agenda (~Do task <2026-10-11 Sun +14d>~ shows as ~Do task~; each day of a range shows ~(day 2/3)~). ~nil~ shows the title as written. Emacs removes only a time of day; this removes the whole stamp |
| ~org-agenda-show-inherited-tags~ | ~t~ | Whether Agenda and TODO list rows show inherited tags, dimmed after the title |
| ~org-agenda-skip-archived-trees~ | ~t~ | Exclude archived headings (tagged ~:ARCHIVE:~) from the agenda; ~nil~ includes them |
| ~org-agenda-skip-comment-trees~ | ~t~ | Exclude commented headings (~** COMMENT draft~) from the agenda. They stay visible in the outline; ~nil~ includes them |
| ~org-agenda-sorting-strategy~ | unset | Only ~effort-up~ and ~effort-down~ are read, from the ~agenda~ and ~todo~ entries: ~((agenda effort-up) (todo effort-down))~ starts the list sorted by effort |
| ~org-agenda-start-on-weekday~ | ~1~ (Monday) | The Week view's first day: ~0~ is Sunday through ~6~ Saturday. An out-of-range value falls back to Monday |
| ~org-agenda-tag-filter-preset~ | unset | Tag chip to start with: ~("+work" "-later")~. Several ~+~ tags must all be present; a ~-~ tag hides its headings |
| ~org-agenda-text-search-extra-files~ | unset | More files for text search only, in the same syntax as ~org-agenda-files~ (see [[#search-extra-files][Search extra files]]) |
| ~org-ascii-charset~ | ~ascii~ | Characters used by ASCII export: ~ascii~, ~latin1~ or ~utf-8~ |
| ~org-ascii-text-width~ | ~72~ | Wrap width, in characters, for ASCII export |
| ~org-babel-load-languages~ | ~((emacs-lisp . t))~ | ~(js . t)~ in the list lets ~js~ source blocks run (see [[#source-blocks][Source blocks]]); read from Global Variables only, never from a file; also Settings → Quick Settings → *Editing* |
| ~org-cite-basic-author-year-separator~ | ~, ~ | Text between author and year in a citation |
| ~org-cite-basic-sorting-field~ | ~author~ | Field the reference list is sorted by |
| ~org-cite-global-bibliography~ | unset | Bibliography files used by every document, as a Lisp list of paths (see [[#citations][Citations]]) |
| ~org-closed-keep-when-no-todo~ | ~nil~ | ~t~ keeps a CLOSED timestamp when a DONE heading is cycled back to no keyword. Cycling to another keyword always removes it (see [[#progress-logging][Progress logging]]) |
| ~org-contacts-birthday-property~ | ~BIRTHDAY~ | The property ~org-contacts-anniversaries~ reads, as a plain string (~# org-contacts-birthday-property: EVENT~) |
| ~org-contacts-files~ | unset (current file only) | More files for [[#export][Contacts (.vcf)]] export (see [[#contacts-files][Contacts Files]]) |
| ~org-cycle-open-archived-trees~ | ~nil~ | ~nil~: an archived heading starts folded whatever ~#+STARTUP:~ says, and the swipe gesture refuses to open it (the chevron still does, as org's force-open commands do). ~t~ makes archived headings behave like any other |
| ~org-deadline-warning-days~ | ~14~ | How many days before its date a DEADLINE with no warning suffix starts showing in the agenda |
| ~org-footnote-auto-adjust~ | ~nil~ | After adding or deleting a footnote: ~renumber~ fn:N, ~sort~ the definitions, both (~t~) or neither |
| ~org-footnote-auto-label~ | ~t~ | Label for a new footnote: ~t~ next number, ~confirm~ next number you can edit, ~nil~ ask, ~random~ |
| ~org-footnote-define-inline~ | ~nil~ | Write new footnotes as ~[fn:label:text]~ at the reference |
| ~org-footnote-section~ | ~Footnotes~ | Heading that holds footnote definitions; ~nil~ puts each at the end of its own section (see [[#footnotes][Footnote commands]]) |
| ~org-global-properties~ | unset | Properties that apply everywhere. Only ~Effort_ALL~ is used, as in ~Effort_ALL: 0:15 0:30 1:00 2:00~ (see [[#effort-all][Effort_ALL]]) |
| ~org-html-head~ | unset | A quoted string added to the ~<head>~ of every HTML export; a file's own ~#+HTML_HEAD:~ is added after it. Settings → Export sets it |
| ~org-html-postamble~ | ~auto~ | A quoted format string for the foot of every HTML export, or ~nil~ for none. A file's own ~#+OPTIONS: html-postamble:~ wins |
| ~org-html-preamble~ | unset (none) | A quoted format string shown above the content of every HTML export (~%t~ title, ~%s~ subtitle, ~%a~ author, ~%d~ date, ~%e~ email). A file's own ~#+OPTIONS: html-preamble:~ wins |
| ~org-latex-compiler~ | ~pdflatex~ | ~pdflatex~, ~xelatex~ or ~lualatex~, for files with no ~#+LATEX_COMPILER:~ |
| ~org-latex-default-class~ | ~article~ | ~article~, ~report~ or ~book~: the class of every LaTeX export whose file has no ~#+LATEX_CLASS:~. Settings → Export sets it |
| ~org-log-done~ | ~nil~ (no logging) | ~'time~ inserts a ~CLOSED:~ timestamp when a heading becomes DONE; ~'note~ also asks for a note, kept in a ~:LOGBOOK:~ drawer. Its ~#+STARTUP:~ shorthands are ~logdone~ and ~lognotedone~ (see [[#progress-logging][Progress logging]] for the per-keyword ~!~ and ~@~ forms) |
| ~org-refile-targets~ | current file, level 1 | Which headings Refile offers, such as ~current maxlevel=3; notes.org tag=work level=2; agenda-files todo=NEXT~ (see [[#refile][Refile]]) |
| ~org-startup-folded~ | ~showeverything~ | The initial visibility: ~'overview~, ~'content~, ~'showall~, ~'showeverything~ or ~'show2levels~ to ~'show5levels~ (the quote is optional); see [[#folding-and-startup][Folding]] |
| ~org-startup-with-inline-images~ | ~nil~ | Whether images render inline when a file opens |
| ~org-table-duration-hour-zero-padding~ | ~t~ | Whether the ~T~ and ~U~ duration flags zero-pad the hours (see [[#table-formulas][Table formulas]]) |
| ~org-tags-exclude-from-inheritance~ | (none) | Tags that never inherit, as a list (~("private")~) or just words (~private archive~) |
| ~org-use-property-inheritance~ | ~nil~ | ~t~ lets a ~key:value~ search filter also match a value inherited from an ancestor (a heading's own value wins). A ~t~ or ~nil~ simplification of org's fuller value space |
| ~org-use-sub-superscripts~ | ~t~ | ~t~, ~{}~ or ~nil~ (three values, as in org); see [[#inline-text-markup][Inline text markup]]. An unrecognized value falls back to ~t~ |
| ~org-use-tag-inheritance~ | ~t~ | ~t~ lets a ~tag:~ search filter match a tag inherited from an ancestor; ~nil~ limits it to the heading's own tags; a list such as ~("work" "home")~ or a quoted regexp such as ~"^proj_"~ inherits only those tags. Applies to search, the Agenda tag filters and the tags shown on a heading |
| ~org-weather-format~ | ~"Weather: %desc, %tcur(%tmin-%tmax)%tu, %p%pu, %h%hu, %s%su, %a%au"~ | (own) The template ~%%(org-weather)~ fills in (see [[#agenda-diary-sexp][Diary-sexp forms]]) |
| ~org-weather-refresh-interval~ | ~never~ | (own) ~never~, or an automatic refresh every ~1~, ~2~, ~4~, ~6~, ~12~ or ~24~ hours |
| ~org-weather-speed-unit~ | ~mph~ | (own) ~km/h~, ~m/s~, ~mph~ or ~Knots~ |
| ~org-weather-temperature-unit~ | ~°F~ | (own) ~°C~ or ~°F~ |
| ~org-xx-drag-handle~ | ~right~ | (own) Where the drag grip sits on a heading row: ~right~, ~left~ or ~off~; also Settings → Quick Settings → *Keyboard* |
| ~org-xx-extensions~ | ~off~ | (own) ~on~ lets the approved init script run (see [[#extensions][Extensions]]); read from Global Variables only, never from a file; also Settings → Quick Settings → *Editing* |
| ~org-xx-extra-menu~ | unset (button hidden) | (own) The floating extras (☰) button's menu (see [[#extras-menu][Extras menu]]) |
| ~org-xx-god-mode-button~ | ~t~ (shown) | (own) Whether the floating *[g]* god-mode button is shown (see [[#god-mode-mobile][God-mode without a hardware keyboard]]); also Settings → Quick Settings → *Keyboard* |
| ~org-xx-latex-header~ | unset | (own) A quoted string of preamble lines added to every LaTeX export before the file's own ~#+LATEX_HEADER:~ lines. Settings → Export → LaTeX fills it for *Fix wide TOC numbers* |
| ~org-xx-menu-aliases~ | unset (no relabeling) | (own) Relabel or hide buttons across the File, More, Export, Import and View menus (see [[#menu-customization][Menu customization]]) |
| ~org-xx-show-inherited-tags~ | ~t~ | (own) Whether the outline shows inherited tags, dimmed with a dashed border, after a heading's own |
| ~org-xx-startup-with-show-photos~ | ~nil~ | (own) ~t~ shows a contact's photo as a thumbnail beside its field when a file opens: next to ~:PHOTO:~ in Flat style, in the "Photo" sub-heading's drawer in Tree style. It follows that field's visibility, so a collapsed contact or folded drawer shows no photo. It has no ~#+STARTUP:~ keyword (see [[#export][Contacts (.vcf) export]]) |
| ~solar-ampm~ | ~nil~ (24-hour) | (own) ~t~ uses 12-hour am/pm for the solar forms |
| ~solar-hide-label~ | ~nil~ (label shown) | (own) ~t~ drops the trailing label ("Sunrise", "daylight") and shows the bare time or duration |

Any other ~# key: value~ line is parsed and ignored, so new variables can be added later without changing the format.

-----

** Progress logging
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: progress-logging
:END:

Two mechanisms write into a heading's ~:LOGBOOK:~ drawer, org's running history of state changes and notes, kept apart from the body.

*** ~org-log-done~

Set by ~#+STARTUP: logdone~ or ~lognotedone~ (see [[#folding-and-startup][Folding and #+STARTUP]]), it controls what happens when a heading becomes DONE. The two are mutually exclusive:

- ~logdone~ (~time~) inserts a ~CLOSED: [timestamp]~ line. Cycling to a non-done keyword removes it, and so does cycling back to no keyword unless ~org-closed-keep-when-no-todo~ is set (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]). Switching between two done keywords (DONE to KILL) leaves it alone.
- ~lognotedone~ (~note~) prompts for a note when a heading becomes DONE; the badge flips at once, so *Skip* only declines the note. A saved note becomes a timestamped ~:LOGBOOK:~ entry.

They apply to a done keyword with no logging spec of its own. With neither, as by default in org, entering DONE adds nothing extra.

*** The per-keyword logging spec

The per-keyword spec applies to any keyword, not only done ones, and overrides ~org-log-done~ for it. It uses the parenthesized fast-key syntax in ~#+TODO:~:

#+BEGIN_SRC
#+TODO: TODO(t) WAIT(w@/!) | DONE(d!) KILL(k@)
#+END_SRC

Four markers, each optional, as in org:

| Marker | Meaning |
|---+---|
| ~!~ | Log a timestamp when *entering* this state |
| ~@~ | Log a note (prompted for, same panel as ~org-log-done~'s own) when *entering* this state |
| ~@/!~ | Log a note when entering, /and/ a timestamp when *leaving* — conditionally, see below |
| ~/!~ | Log a timestamp only when *leaving* this state — no logging on entering it at all |

A leaving-log (~@/!~ or ~/!~) fires only if the target state doesn't already log on entry. In the example, WAIT to DONE adds nothing from WAIT's ~/!~, because DONE logs a timestamp on entry (~d!~); WAIT to TODO does, since TODO logs nothing and the move would go unrecorded. A ~CLOSED~ timestamp and a ~:LOGBOOK:~ entry can both fire for one transition, as in org.


*Fast-access keys* (the letter in ~TODO(t)~) are parsed, so a ~#+TODO:~ line using them still works. A ~#+TODO:~ line with no ~|~ treats its last keyword as the only done state, as in org.

*Parallel workflows*: several ~#+TODO:~ lines (~#+TODO: TODO(t) | DONE(d)~ then ~#+TODO: REPORT(r) BUG(b) | FIXED(f)~) define coexisting workflows. The badge cycles within the sequence a heading's keyword belongs to. For a heading with no state, the badge, the *TODO* button and ~C-c C-t~ cycle with one workflow and open a picker of every state of every workflow with more than one (first states green, done states red; *Clear* blanks the heading, *Cancel* dismisses). ~#+SEQ_TODO:~ and ~#+TYP_TODO:~ are read like ~#+TODO:~.

*** The ~:LOGBOOK:~ drawer

Shown under a heading like ~:PROPERTIES:~, with the same visibility rule (hidden unless ~#+STARTUP: showeverything~ or the heading is swiped fully open). A state change shows the transition and timestamp (~WAIT → DONE   [timestamp]~) with any note indented beneath. ~CLOCK:~ lines show as ~Clock: start–end ⇒ duration~ once closed and ~Clock: start (running)~ while open (see [[#clocking][Clocking]]).

*** Agenda: Log

The Agenda's date-range line has a *Log* checkbox, off by default (org's ~org-agenda-log-mode~). On, every ~:LOGBOOK:~ entry in the aggregated files appears as its own dated item with a 📝 icon and any note, including the history of DONE headings that the Agenda otherwise hides.

-----

** Archiving
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: archiving
:END:

Tap a heading's title, then *Archive*, to move its subtree to the archive location (org's ~org-archive-subtree~, ~C-c C-x C-s~). A panel shows the destination and what will be added (*Archive & details*) and places to refile to instead (*Refile & details*, see [[#refile][Refile]]); *Cancel* has focus, so a stray tap does nothing.

The moved heading gets an ~:ARCHIVE:~ tag and properties recording where it came from (~ARCHIVE_TIME~, ~ARCHIVE_FILE~, ~ARCHIVE_OLPATH~, ~ARCHIVE_CATEGORY~, ~ARCHIVE_TODO~, ~ARCHIVE_ITAGS~). The original is removed only after the copy is safely written.

The location is ~org-archive-location~: the heading's own ~ARCHIVE~ property, else the file's ~#+ARCHIVE:~ keyword, else ~%s_archive::~. It is a file (~%s~ is the current file's name; empty means the current file) and an optional heading, joined by ~::~, where the stars give the heading's level (~* Archived Tasks~).

| Location | Behavior |
|---+---|
| ~%s_archive::~ (default) | Sibling file ~notes.org_archive~, top-level entries |
| ~::* Archived Tasks~ | Same file, filed under a top-level ~* Archived Tasks~ heading (created if it doesn't exist yet) |
| ~~/org/archive.org::~ | One central file, top-level entries |
| ~~/org/archive.org::* %s~ | One central file, filed under a heading named after the source file |

Archiving to a different file works on GitHub and WebDAV only (a local or iOS-imported file needs a file picker the browser won't show mid-archive); within the current file it works everywhere. Not supported: ~datetree/~ targets and multi-level heading paths.

*** Restoring (unarchive)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: restoring-unarchive
:END:

Open the archive file (*File → Open* lists ~_archive~ files), tap the archived heading, then *Unarchive*. The same panel opens with *Restore*; the heading moves back to its original file and place, loses ~:ARCHIVE:~ and the ~ARCHIVE_*~ properties, and gets its TODO state back from ~ARCHIVE_TODO~.

A heading tagged ~:ARCHIVE:~ by hand, with no recorded ~ARCHIVE_FILE~, just has the tag and properties stripped in place. The palette command is *Unarchive (restore)* (~org-unarchive-subtree~); there is no separate list for browsing the archive.

*** Refile
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: refile
:END:

Tap a heading's title, then *Archive*, pick a target in the lower part of the panel and tap *Refile* to move the subtree elsewhere in the outline or into another file (org's ~org-refile~, also in the palette). Targets show their full outline path, with a search box (every word must match), your last five under *RECENT* and the rest under *ALL TARGETS*. The subtree becomes the target's last child with its levels adjusted, and is never offered as its own destination.

Targets come from ~org-refile-targets~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]); the default is the current file's top-level headings. Entries are separated by ~;~, each a file followed by criteria:

#+BEGIN_SRC
org-refile-targets: current maxlevel=3; notes.org tag=work level=2; agenda-files todo=NEXT
#+END_SRC

- *File*: ~current~, ~agenda-files~, or a file name (a bare name is a sibling of the current file), optionally with a ~github:~, ~webdav:~ or ~local:~ prefix, like ~local:inbox.org level=1~.
- *Criteria*: ~level=N~, ~maxlevel=N~, ~tag=NAME~ (the heading's own tag; inheritance is not considered), ~todo=KEYWORD~, and ~regexp=PATTERN~ (matched against the whole heading line, so it must come last; write a literal ~;~ as ~\;~). Several criteria on one entry must all match, which goes beyond real org.

An entry the app can't understand is skipped and listed with the reason at the top of the picker. Refiling to another file works on GitHub and WebDAV; a local file must have been opened once, except in the [[#android-app][Android app]] where a file in the org-pwa folder works. Not built: creating a new heading as the destination.

-----


** Extensions
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: extensions
:END:

An init script can add your own diary functions. Set *Run extension scripts* to ~On~ in Quick Settings, paste the script under Settings → *Extensions*, and tap *Approve and run*. The script stays on this device (it is not synced, exported or read from any file), and editing it withdraws the approval.

~org.sexp(name, fn)~: makes ~%%(name args)~ work in an agenda file. ~fn~ is called once per day with ~ctx~ (~date~, ~year~, ~month~, ~day~, ~weekday~ with 0 for Sunday, ~today~, ~calendarLatitude~, ~calendarLongitude~) and then your arguments as plain values. Return ~true~ for an entry with the line's own text, a string for an entry with that text, anything else for none.

#+BEGIN_SRC
org.sexp("every-other-friday", (ctx, start) => {
  const days = (Date.parse(ctx.date) - Date.parse(start)) / 86400000;
  return days >= 0 && days % 14 === 0;
});
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC
,* Pay day
%%(every-other-friday "2026-01-02") Pay day
#+END_SRC

~org.command(id, label, fn)~: adds *label* to the command palette. ~fn(ctx)~ gets ~ctx.heading~, the heading the command was run on (or null), and can read the whole file through ~org.document~: its ~name~ and its ~headings~, each with ~index~, ~level~, ~title~, ~todo~, ~priority~, ~tags~, ~properties~, ~scheduled~, ~deadline~, ~closed~, ~body~ and ~path~. It changes the file with ~org.edit~: ~setTitle~, ~setTodo~, ~setTags~, ~setProperty~, ~deleteProperty~ and ~appendBody~, each taking a heading's ~index~. The edits are checked, then applied together as one undo step; none is applied if one is invalid, the buffer is read-only or the file changed while the command ran. ~org.notify(text)~, or a string returned from ~fn~, shows a message in the status line.

#+BEGIN_SRC
org.command("tag-urgent", "Tag as urgent", (ctx) => {
  if (!ctx.heading) return "Put the cursor on a heading first";
  org.edit.setTags(ctx.heading.index, [...ctx.heading.tags, "urgent"]);
});
#+END_SRC

~org.on(event, fn)~: runs ~fn(ctx)~ when something happens. The events are ~open~ (a file finished loading), ~save~ (a save succeeded), ~todo-change~ (a heading's TODO state changed; ~ctx.heading~, ~ctx.from~ and ~ctx.to~) and ~capture~ (a capture was filed; ~ctx.description~, ~ctx.file~). A hook can use ~org.notify~ in any event, and ~org.edit~ after ~todo-change~ and ~capture~; its edits are one separate undo step, and do not set hooks off again. Edits after ~save~ or ~open~ are ignored, since they would mark the file modified the moment it was saved or opened. A hook that fails is logged and never blocks saving or opening.

#+BEGIN_SRC
org.on("todo-change", (ctx) => {
  if (ctx.to === "DONE") org.edit.setProperty(ctx.heading.index, "FINISHED", new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10));
});
#+END_SRC

A name is letters, digits and dashes, and ~org.sexp~ cannot take a standard form such as ~diary-float~. The script runs in the same sandbox as ~js~ blocks. A diary function that takes longer than 3 seconds, a command longer than 5, or a hook longer than 2, stops the script. Emacs does not know your functions, so a file that uses one needs the same function defined in Emacs Lisp to work there. Not built: the rest of the planned API.

*** Table functions, link types and exports
- ~org.tableFunction(name, fn)~: use ~name(...)~ in a ~#+TBLFM:~ formula. Arguments are numbers or text; return a number or text. Run with the table's Calc button or /Recalculate all tables/.
- ~org.linkType(prefix, fn)~: makes ~[[prefix:path][label]]~ clickable. ~fn(path)~ returns an address (https, mailto, tel or geo) that is opened.
- ~org.exportBackend(id, label, fn)~: adds /Export: label/ to the palette. ~fn(ctx)~ gets ~ctx.document~ and returns text, or ~{ text, filename, mime }~ (up to 2 MB).

#+begin_src js
org.tableFunction("twice", (n) => n * 2);
org.linkType("weather", (place) => "https://wttr.in/" + encodeURIComponent(place));
org.exportBackend("titles", "Titles only", (ctx) => ctx.document.headings.map((h) => h.title).join("\n"));
#+end_src

*** Agenda sources and header lines
- ~org.agenda.source(name, fn)~: ~fn({ from, to })~ returns items for the agenda, each ~{ title, start, end, repeat }~ with ~start~ as ~"2026-12-25"~ or ~"2026-12-25 09:30"~ and ~repeat~ such as ~"+1w"~. Asked again after ten minutes.
- ~await org.ics.parse(text)~: the events of a calendar feed as ~{ summary, start, end, allDay, location, repeat, cancelled }~. Complex recurrences are not expanded.
- ~org.ui.line(id, fn)~: ~fn()~ returns one line of text shown above the agenda.

#+begin_src js
org.agenda.source("holidays", async () => {
  const r = await org.fetch("https://example.org/us-holidays.ics");
  return org.ics.parse(await r.text());
});
org.ui.line("mood", () => "Have a good day");
#+end_src

*** Network, position and cache
The sandbox has no network, but a script or a ~js~ block can ask the page:
- ~await org.fetch(url, { method, headers, body })~ returns ~{ status, ok, url, text(), json() }~. Only https (or http to this device), GET or POST, the headers Accept, Content-Type, Authorization and X-Api-Key, a body up to 100 KB, no cookies, 8 seconds, up to 1 MB back, 30 requests per run. A redirect to a host you did not allow is refused.
- ~await org.location.get()~ returns ~{ lat, lon, accuracy, time }~, rounded to about 10 m.
- ~await org.cache.get(key, maxAgeMs)~ returns a stored value or ~null~; ~await org.cache.set(key, value)~ stores one (200 KB each, 1 MB and 100 keys per script or document) and returns it.
You are asked before the first use. A block lists what it needs: ~#+BEGIN_SRC js :net api.open-meteo.com :location yes~ (several hosts separated by spaces; ~*.example.org~ covers subdomains) and you are asked once per document. The init script is asked per host and for the position when it first uses them. The question warns that the code can send anything it can read, including the open file, to the site, so allow only code you trust.

-----

** Source blocks
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: source-blocks
:END:

~js~ blocks run in place, as in Org Babel. They are off until you set *Run JavaScript source blocks* to ~On~ in Settings → Quick Settings → *Editing*. The setting comes from your Global Variables, never from a file, so a document cannot turn it on for itself.

Each ~js~ block then has a *Run* button; ~C-c C-c~ or the palette's *Run source block* runs the block under the cursor. The result is written under it as ~#+RESULTS:~ and replaced on the next run; one Undo removes it.

#+BEGIN_SRC
,#+NAME: sales
| q  |  n |
|----+----|
| Q1 | 10 |
| Q2 | 20 |

,#+BEGIN_SRC js :var data=sales
return data.slice(1).map(([q, n]) => [q, n * 2]);
,#+END_SRC

,#+RESULTS:
| Q1 | 20 |
| Q2 | 40 |
#+END_SRC

- ~:results~: ~value~ (the default: what the block ~return~s) or ~output~ (the ~console.log~ lines), with ~table~, ~list~, ~raw~ or ~silent~.
- ~:var name=value~: a number, a quoted string, or the ~#+NAME:~ of a table, which arrives as an array of rows.
- ~:timeout N~: seconds, 5 by default and 60 at most. A block still running then is stopped.
- ~:wrap NAME~: wraps the result in a ~#+begin_NAME~ block.

The code runs in a sandbox with no access to the page, your files or your accounts, and no network unless the header asks and you allow it (see Network, position and cache). ~org.vars.get("calendar-latitude")~ reads a setting. The first run in a saved document asks for confirmation; an unsaved one asks every time.


*** Literate programming: header arguments, Noweb and Tangle
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: literate-programming
:END:

Header arguments are inherited as in Org: ~#+PROPERTY: header-args :results output~ applies to the whole file, ~header-args:js~ to ~js~ blocks only, and a ~:header-args:~ property to a subtree (~header-args+~ adds instead of replacing). A block's own arguments and ~#+HEADER:~ lines win.

*Noweb*: with ~:noweb yes~, ~<<name>>~ in a block is replaced by the block ~#+NAME: name~, by all blocks with ~:noweb-ref name~ (joined with ~:noweb-sep~, a newline by default), or by the text of the heading whose ~CUSTOM_ID~ is ~name~. Text before the reference on its line is put before every line of the expansion, so ~// <<name>>~ comments out all of it. ~:noweb~ also takes ~tangle~, ~no-export~ (expand to run and tangle, show the references on export), ~strip-export~ (references removed on export) and ~strip-tangle~. ~yes~ expands when running, tangling and exporting. A reference that matches nothing, or that goes round in a circle, is an error rather than empty text.

*Tangle*: the palette command *Tangle this file* (~org-babel-tangle~) writes the blocks with ~:tangle~ to files: ~:tangle yes~ names the file after the document, ~:tangle path/file.js~ names it, ~no~ skips it. Blocks for the same file are joined in order, separated by a blank line (~:padline no~ removes it). Also supported: ~:shebang~ (and the file mode that goes with it), ~:tangle-mode~, ~:comments link~, ~org~, ~both~ and ~noweb~ (which also wraps each ~<<name>>~ chunk in comments naming the block it came from), ~:prologue~, ~:epilogue~, ~:no-expand~, and ~:var~ for ~js~ blocks (written as ~var x=3;~). ~COMMENT~ and ~:ARCHIVE:~ subtrees are skipped. One file is saved as it is; several, or one in a folder, come as a zip with the file modes set. Paths may not be absolute or climb out with ~..~. The output was checked against Emacs's own.
