*Cache*: ~:cache yes~ skips a block whose code, variables and ~:results~ are unchanged since its last run (the hash sits in ~#+RESULTS[hash]:~). Delete the results to force a run. Don't cache a block that reads the time or a live feed.

*Export* follows ~:exports~: ~code~ (the default), ~results~, ~both~ or ~none~. Nothing is run on export; ~results~ shows what ~#+RESULTS:~ already holds. This covers ASCII, HTML, LaTeX, Markdown, ODT and Org export.

*The init script from an Org file*: in Settings → Extensions, *Use an Org file…* takes ~github:path~, ~webdav:path~ or ~local:name~, then ~::target~ (default ~::init.js~). The blocks of that file that tangle to the target become the init script, Noweb included. Only the file you name is read; the approval covers the assembled text, so a change to the file asks again.

-----

** Attachments
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: attachments
:END:

Files kept with a heading, as in Org's ~org-attach~. Press ~C-c C-a~ on a heading, or tap *Attach* in 📋 Edit details, for a grid of buttons:

- *Attach* (~a~): on a phone or tablet, opens the system chooser to pick files or photos, or take a photo or video; the file is copied into the heading's folder. On ChromeOS and desktop it first asks *Choose a file*, *Take a photo* or *Record a video* (the last two use an in-app webcam panel).
- *Record audio* (~r~): record from the microphone, play it back, then save.
- *Attach open document* (~b~, ~org-attach-buffer~): save one of your open documents, as text, in the folder.
- *New text file* (~n~, ~org-attach-new~): give a name and type its contents.
- *Open* (~o~): show a picture, recording, video or text file inside the app; anything else opens in the browser's viewer, or downloads when there is none.
- *Folder* (~f~, ~org-attach-reveal~): the folder as a list with a checkbox per file, then ~O~ (open), ~S~ (save to disk) and ~D~ (delete). The strip above acts on the selection and adds files.
- *Delete one* (~d~) and *Delete all* (~D~): remove files after a confirmation.
- *Set DIR* (~s~) and *Unset DIR* (~S~): keep a heading's files in a folder of your choosing instead. Unset DIR asks whether to move the files to the ID folder, delete them, or leave them.
- *Sync* (~z~, ~org-attach-sync~): set the ~:ATTACH:~ tag to match what is in the folder, for files added or removed by other means.

Each heading's files live in ~data/<first 2 characters of its ID>/<rest of the ID>/~ beside the document; the heading gets an ~ID~ property and an ~:ATTACH:~ tag the first time. A ~DIR~ property names another folder, relative to the document (a leading ~/~ starts at the storage root) and wins over the ID. A file added to the folder by other means shows up too. With several files, Open, Preview, Save and Delete ask which one.

Example: on a heading, ~C-c C-a~, then ~a~, pick ~receipt.pdf~. The heading now carries ~:ATTACH:~ and ~receipt.pdf~ is in its folder.

*Links in the body*: Settings → Attachments chooses whether attaching also adds an ~[[attachment:name]]~ link: for pictures, audio and video (the default), always, or never. A bare link to a picture shows it inline; audio gets a play button. Tapping an ~attachment:~ link does what *Open* does. A link finds its folder from its heading's ~ID~, else the nearest ancestor's.

*Requirements*: GitHub or WebDAV must be connected. The [[#android-app][Android app]] instead keeps a local file's attachments in the org-pwa folder you choose once.

*Large files*: over 25MB asks before attaching (the whole file is held in memory). GitHub refuses over 95MB, so use WebDAV for long videos.

*Filenames*: unsafe characters become ~_~; a duplicate gets ~-1~, ~-2~ before the extension.

*Not built*: Org's copy/move/link variants (~c~, ~m~, ~l~) and absolute ~DIR~ paths outside the storage.

-----

** Clocking
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: clocking
:END:

Every clocking action is a [[#command-palette][command palette]] command: *Clock in*, *Clock out*, *Cancel clock*, *Continue last clock*, *Go to clocked task* and *Set effort estimate*, found by name or by Org name (~org-clock-in~ and so on). One clock runs at a time.

- *org-clock-in* inserts a bare ~CLOCK: [timestamp]~ line on the heading whose action menu is open, else the focused one. On the heading already clocked it does nothing; on another it clocks the running one out at the same moment.
- *org-clock-out* turns the line into ~CLOCK: [start]--[end] =>  H:MM~. *org-clock-cancel* removes the running line and records nothing. Both act on whichever clock is running; with none they say so.
- *org-clock-in-last* (~C-c C-x C-x~; palette *Continue last clock*, ~c x x~ in god-mode) resumes clocking the most recently clocked heading. In an Extras entry it is ~'org-clock-in-last~ (see [[#extras-menu][Extras Menu]]).
- *org-clock-goto* (~C-c C-x C-j~; palette *Go to clocked task*, ~c x j~) jumps to the clocked heading from any tab, unfolding what hides it. With ~C-u~ (~u c x j~, or the palette's *Go to a recently clocked task*, ~org-clock-select-task~) it lists recently clocked tasks from every open tab, newest first.

Clock lines live in a ~:LOGBOOK:~ drawer from the first one. Org itself keeps the first one bare (see [[#progress-logging][Progress logging]]).

*Showing clocked time*:

- *org-clock-display*: a *Clock* checkbox on *View → TODO* (like Agenda's *Log*; see [[#agenda][Agenda]]) shows each item's total clocked time beside its title: all time ever clocked on the task and its descendants, including a running clock's elapsed time. It is off by default and is a session toggle, not a variable.
- *org-clock-report*: a ~#+BEGIN: clocktable ... #+END:~ block, computed for a date range and shown read-only under *View → TODO*'s *Clock report* (see [[#the-todo-view][The TODO view]]).
- While a clock runs, the modeline (see [[#modeline][Modeline and minibuffer]]) shows ~[⏱ H:MM] Heading title~, refreshed every 30 seconds.

*Effort estimates*: *Set effort estimate* (~C-c C-x e~, ~org-set-effort~) prompts for the ~EFFORT~ of the open or focused heading. Any ~org-duration~ form works, stored as typed: ~1:30~; ~2h~, ~45min~, ~1d 3h~; ~2.35h~; or a bare number of minutes. Units are Emacs's defaults: ~min~, ~h~, ~d~ (24 h), ~w~ (7 d), ~m~ (a *month* of 30 days, so write ~30min~ for half an hour) and ~y~. A blank value clears it; an invalid one is refused. You can also type it into *Edit details → Properties*.

An ~EFFORT~ shows beside the title as a ~⏱~ badge; tapping it opens the same prompt. While that heading is clocked in, the modeline shows ~[⏱ 0:45 / 2:00] Heading title~, with a trailing ~!~ once the estimate is passed.

Not built: custom duration units (~org-duration-units~), the ~Effort_ALL+~ append form, and a reminder tied to the estimate beyond the modeline's ~!~. See [[#differences-from-emacs-org-mode][Differences from Emacs org-mode]].

-----

*** Effort_ALL: allowed effort values
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: effort-all
:END:

Org's effort prompt completes against a list of allowed values, ~Effort_ALL~. It looks in this order, and the first source that gives at least one usable value wins:

1. an ~Effort_ALL~ property on the heading itself, or on the nearest ancestor that has one;
2. the file's ~#+PROPERTY: Effort_ALL 0 0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00~ line;
3. the *Global properties* setting (~org-global-properties~, in Settings → Advanced or a file's Local Variables): semicolon-separated ~NAME: value~ entries, such as ~Effort_ALL: 0:15 0:30 1:00 2:00 4:00~. Only ~Effort_ALL~ is used.

Values are space-separated, and each must be a valid ~org-duration~ (see [[#clocking][Clocking]]); anything else is skipped. When a list applies, *Set effort estimate* shows its values as buttons above the text box: one tap saves that value, and the box still takes any other duration. With no list the prompt is plain free text. The same list supplies the Agenda's effort filter (see [[#agenda][Agenda]]); with none defined, the filter uses org's own fallback set (~0 0:10 0:30 1:00 2:00 3:00 4:00 5:00 6:00 7:00~).

Not supported: ~Effort_ALL+~, and quoted values containing spaces.


** Narrowing
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: narrowing
:END:

A heading's action menu has *🔽 Narrow*, which restricts the outline to that heading and its subtree (org's ~C-x n s~; god-mode ~x SPC n s~). On the narrowed heading it becomes *🔼 Widen* (~C-x n w~, ~x SPC n w~), and a banner, *Narrowed to: TITLE — Widen*, stays at the top. Narrowing to another heading replaces the restriction.

Narrowing only restricts the display; the file is untouched, and Save, Export, Agenda and Search still use the whole document. It follows its heading through promote, demote, move and rename, and widens if the heading is deleted. It persists across tabs and restarts.


*Text view while narrowed* shows only the narrowed subtree's raw text (see [[#the-plain-text-editor][The plain-text editor]]); switching to Text without narrowing shows the whole file.

-----

** The plain-text editor
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: the-plain-text-editor
:END:

Tap *View → Text* to replace the outline with one textarea holding the raw org text, including ~#+STARTUP:~, ~#+TODO:~, a [[#local-variables][Local Variables]] block and syntax the outline has no UI for. Tap *View → Org* to switch back; the text is reparsed then, so changes take effect at once and count as edits.

*Position*: switching in lands near your last navigation (a search result, internal link or agenda item), approximately; manual scrolling isn't tracked. While [[#narrowing][narrowed]], it starts at the top of the narrowed text.

*Narrowed*: only the narrowed subtree is editable, and switching back splices it into place. Retyping asterisks, renaming or adding headings inside it can't touch anything outside; narrowing follows a level or title change.

*Select All* and *Copy All* buttons sit above the textarea for devices without a keyboard (Copy All falls back to selecting if the clipboard is denied). While narrowed they act on the narrowed text.

*Search works here* on the textarea's live raw text, so it can find and replace inside property drawers and ~#+BEGIN_VERSE~ or ~#+BEGIN_QUOTE~ blocks. *Regex* and *Replace* work as in Org view, including the ~y~, ~n~, ~q~, ~.~, ~!~ walk; *Match* mode isn't offered. Replacements stay in the textarea until you leave or Save.

-----

** Agenda
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda
:END:

Tap *View → Agenda* for everything with a date, in Day, Week or Month view. One button cycles the three views. *‹* and *›* step back or forward by the current unit, *Today* jumps to today, and a horizontal swipe does the same as ‹ and ›. Tapping an item returns to the Org view at that item.

*Row actions*: press and hold an item for *Mark done*, *Set state*, *Reschedule*, *Priority*, *Refile* and *Open heading*. Swipe an item to the right to mark it done; *Undo* stays for a few seconds, and a repeating item moves to its next date. They change the open file only: an item from another agenda file offers *Open heading* alone.

*Filter chips* under the controls narrow the list; a chip shows its choice and an ✕ clears it. They last for the session and combine with *and*:

- *Tag*, *State*, *Category*: pick values, then say what they do: show only items with *any* of them, with *all* of them (tags), or hide items with any (Emacs's ~-~ prefix). Tags include inherited ones (~org-use-tag-inheritance~).
- *Search*: an Emacs regular expression (~\(~ ~\)~ group, ~\|~ alternates), not case sensitive, matched against the keyword, title and tags (Emacs's ~=~ filter). A box can hide the matching rows instead.
- *Top heading*: only items under the chosen top-level headings (Emacs's ~^~).
- *Effort* (TODO view): at most, at least or exactly a duration, as in the ⏱ panel.

The chips start from ~org-agenda-tag-filter-preset~, ~org-agenda-category-filter-preset~, ~org-agenda-regexp-filter-preset~ and ~org-agenda-effort-filter-preset~, and the ⏱ panel from ~org-agenda-sorting-strategy~ and ~org-agenda-max-effort~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]).

*Titles*: a timestamp written in a heading's title is left out of its row, since the day and the time column already say it. Set ~org-agenda-remove-times-when-in-prefix~ to ~nil~ to show titles as written.

*Empty days*: every day shows by default, even when nothing is on it. The *g* button toggles ~org-agenda-show-all-dates~ for the session; it is bold while empty days are hidden. The starting value comes from ~org-agenda-show-all-dates~ in [[#local-variables][Local Variables]] or the *Show empty days in Agenda* Quick Setting.

*Weeks*: Week view always shows a full week, Monday to Sunday by default (~org-agenda-start-on-weekday~). Headers show the ISO week number on each week's first day (always in Day view), and the range label shows ~(W36)~ or ~(W31-W36)~.

*Categories*: every item shows a category prefix: the file's ~#+CATEGORY:~ keyword, else its file name without directory or ~.org~. Put the keyword at the top of the file:

#+BEGIN_SRC org
  ,#+CATEGORY: Projects
  * TODO Review weekly goals
    SCHEDULED: <2026-09-07 Mon>
#+END_SRC

*Times*: a timestamp can carry a range, like ~SCHEDULED: <2026-08-31 Mon 08:00-09:00>~. Week and Month views show ~08:00-09:00~; a single time shows as ~08:00 ……~; an untimed SCHEDULED or DEADLINE shows its ~Scheduled:~ or ~Deadline:~ label instead.

*Time grid*: Day view adds org's default hour grid (dashed lines every two hours, 8am to 8pm). Untimed items come first; timed items sit at their time. Week and Month have no grid.

*Effort*: an item with an ~EFFORT~ property (any ~org-duration~ form, see [[#clocking][Clocking]]) shows it after its title, as typed: ~⏱ 1:30~. Each day header shows the day's total on the right (~⏱ 3:30~), with a trailing ~+2?~ for TODOs that have no estimate yet. The [[#the-todo-view][TODO view]] shows ~⏱~ too. How it counts:

- A heading shown twice in one day (scheduled and deadline) counts once. An overdue task carried forward counts toward today.
- An appointment counts when it has an effort. One with neither a TODO keyword nor an effort is not counted in ~+N?~.
- An explicit ~0:00~ is an estimate. An invalid effort counts as missing.
- Logged entries, diary lines and sunrise/sunset lines never count. A day with no estimates shows no total.

*Sorting, filtering and limiting by effort*: the ~⏱~ button in the toolbar opens a panel, the touch version of org's ~effort-up~ and ~effort-down~, ~org-agenda-filter-by-effort~ and ~org-agenda-max-effort~:

- *Sort*: least or most effort first within each day.
- *Filter*: tasks with effort *at most*, *at least* or *exactly* a value from the [[#effort-all][Effort_ALL]] list (or org's default set).
- *Max per day*: keep tasks while the running total stays within, say, ~4:00~.
- *Reset* clears all three.

The rules are org's: *at most* and *at least* are inclusive; a task with no effort counts as high effort (sorts last, dropped by *at most* and *exactly*, kept by *at least*); the limit keeps a prefix of the sorted day, so an unestimated task ends the list; headingless entries (sunrise, anniversaries) are never filtered or counted; the order is sort, limit, filter. These settings last for the session.

*** Dated entry sources
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-dated-entries
:END:

Five kinds of entry show up; they carry forward as in org:

- ~SCHEDULED:~ shows on its date and, until the heading is done, on today as overdue ("3 days overdue"), as in Emacs. A delay suffix (~SCHEDULED: <2026-01-10 Sat -2d>~) hides it on its own date and shows it on today once the delay has passed.
- ~DEADLINE:~ shows on its date, and on today when overdue or inside its warning period ("due in 3 days"). A suffix (~DEADLINE: <2026-01-10 Sat -3d>~) sets the period; otherwise it is ~org-deadline-warning-days~ (default 14; see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]). Overdue and upcoming entries show on today only, and a repeating one counts from its first date.
- *Plain active timestamps* anywhere in a heading's entry (title, body, property values, drawers), such as ~**** Jane Doe <2000-01-01 Sat +1y>~, are listed beside its SCHEDULED or DEADLINE and never carry forward. Inactive ~[...]~ timestamps, comment lines, ~#+~ lines and source, example, export and comment blocks are ignored.
- A *general sexp timestamp* ~<%%(sexp)>~ in the title follows the same rules; see [[#agenda-sexp-timestamps][General sexp timestamps]].
- ~org-contacts-anniversaries~ reads yearly events (birthdays, anniversaries) from contact headings, as Emacs's org-contacts does. The contacts are the headings of your [[#contacts-files][Contacts Files]] (~org-contacts-files~); with none set, the headings of the files you are looking at. A contact's date is a property, written ~YYYY-MM-DD~, with an optional description after it.

#+BEGIN_SRC org
  * John Doe
  :PROPERTIES:
  :BIRTHDAY: 2000-01-01
  :END:

  * Mary Doe
  :PROPERTIES:
  :ANNIVERSARY: 2015-06-15
  :SPOUSE: John Doe
  :END:
#+END_SRC

  A line ~%%(org-contacts-anniversaries FIELD FORMAT)~ in any agenda file is a switch, not an event. ~FIELD~ is the property to read, as a quoted string (~BIRTHDAY~ by default, or ~org-contacts-birthday-property~), and ~FORMAT~ says how each entry reads; either may be left out or written ~nil~. Each distinct line is its own scan, so a plain one and one with ~"ANNIVERSARY"~ give both, in one file or two, and the same line twice is one:

#+BEGIN_SRC org
  %%(org-contacts-anniversaries)
  %%(org-contacts-anniversaries "ANNIVERSARY")
  %%(org-contacts-anniversaries "ANNIVERSARY" "Anniversary: %h & %s (%Y)")
#+END_SRC

  Entries read ~Birthday: John Doe (26th)~, or ~Anniversary: Mary Doe & John Doe (11th)~ for a contact with a ~:SPOUSE:~, with the age worked out for each year shown. In a ~FORMAT~, ~%h~ and ~%l~ are the name, ~%y~ the age, ~%Y~ the age as an ordinal (~26th~), ~%s~ the spouse, ~%n~ the name with the spouse, and ~%%~ a percent sign (~%s~ and ~%n~ are this app's). ~YYYY~ may be ~nil~ when the year is unknown, shown as ~(??)~. Text after the date in the property replaces the label (~:BIRTHDAY: 2000-06-15 Wedding Anniversary~ reads ~Wedding Anniversary: Mary & John Doe (26th)~). A value that can't be parsed is skipped. No ~:EMAIL:~ is required.

  This works with [[#import][vCard import]]. In Flat style the properties are bare dates. In Tree style they are descendant headings (~:FIELDTYPE: birthday~, ~anniversary~ and ~spouse~), found anywhere in the contact's subtree unless the contact has its own property.

*** Diary-sexp forms
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-diary-sexp
:END:

These are self-contained lines anywhere in a heading's body, with no switch line needed. They show with a 🔁 icon (☀️ for the solar ones).

- ~%%(org-anniversary YEAR MONTH DAY) text~: applies only to years after YEAR. In the text, ~%d~ becomes the elapsed years and ~%s~ its ordinal suffix, so ~%%(org-anniversary 2001 6 12) %d%s wedding anniversary~ shows "25th wedding anniversary" in 2026. February 29 counts as March 1 in non-leap years.
- ~%%(org-cyclic N YEAR MONTH DAY) text~: every N days from that date, never before it.
- ~%%(diary-float MONTH DAYNAME N [DAY] [YEAR]) text~: the Nth weekday of a month. MONTH is 1 to 12, a list like ~(1 4 7 10)~ (a quoted ~'(1 4 7 10)~ also works), or ~t~ for every month. DAYNAME is 0 (Sunday) to 6. N counts from the start of the month when positive and from the end when negative (~-1~ is the last). ~%%(diary-float 11 4 4) Thanksgiving~ is the 4th Thursday of November. An optional DAY moves where scanning starts (~%%(diary-float 11 2 1 2) US Election Day~ starts at the 2nd, skipping a Tuesday on the 1st), and an optional YEAR limits the entry to that year.
- ~%%(org-block Y1 M1 D1 Y2 M2 D2) text~: every day in an inclusive range, in either order.
- Lines built from ~and~, ~or~, ~not~, ~when~, ~if~, ~cond~, ~let~, ~org-class~ or ~org-date~, such as ~%%(and (org-block 2026 9 1 2026 12 18) (org-class 2026 9 1 2026 12 18 1)) Seminar~, use the evaluator described under [[#agenda-sexp-timestamps][General sexp timestamps]]. The text after the closing parenthesis is the entry, and a string result replaces it.
- ~%%(diary-sunrise)~, ~diary-sunset~, ~diary-civil-dawn~, ~diary-civil-dusk~, ~diary-nautical-dawn~, ~diary-nautical-dusk~, ~diary-astronomical-dawn~ and ~diary-astronomical-dusk~ are this app's own. They use ~calendar-latitude~ and ~calendar-longitude~ (default Durham, NC; set them in Local Variables or with the device-location button in Quick Settings) and show, for example, "06:30 Sunrise", "20:15 Sunset", "06:02 Dawn", "20:43 Dusk" in 24-hour time. Civil, nautical and astronomical twilight are the sun 6°, 12° and 18° below the horizon; ~n/a~ replaces the time on a day when it doesn't occur. ~solar-ampm~ (default ~nil~) switches to 12-hour ("6:30am Sunrise") and ~solar-hide-label~ (default ~nil~) drops the label ("06:30"); set them in Local Variables or Quick Settings ([[#settings][Settings]]).
- ~%%(diary-day-length)~ shows the day's daylight as "13:32 daylight". ~solar-hide-label~ applies and ~solar-ampm~ doesn't. Polar day and night show "24:00" and "00:00".
- ~%%(org-weather)~ shows current conditions and today's forecast from [[https://open-meteo.com/][Open-Meteo]] (free, no key), for the same coordinates. It is one entry, on today only, showing the last-fetched snapshot, and nothing until the first refresh.

~org-weather-format~ controls the text. The default is ~"Weather: %desc, %tcur(%tmin-%tmax)%tu, %p%pu, %h%hu, %s%su, %a%au"~, which gives "Weather: Overcast, 86.3(75.5-91.8)°F, 1002.8hPa, 49%, 5.1mph, 12m". An unrecognized ~%~ sequence is left as is.

| Placeholder | Meaning |
|---+---|
| ~%desc~, ~%icon~ | Description and emoji for the current weather code |
| ~%tcur~, ~%tmin~, ~%tmax~ | Current temperature, today's low and high |
| ~%tamin~, ~%tamax~ | Today's "feels like" low and high |
| ~%tu~ | Temperature unit (~org-weather-temperature-unit~, default ~°F~) |
| ~%h~, ~%hu~ | Humidity and its unit |
| ~%p~, ~%pu~ | Surface pressure and its unit (~hPa~) |
| ~%s~, ~%su~ | Wind speed and unit (~org-weather-speed-unit~: ~mph~ by default, ~km/h~, ~m/s~ or ~Knots~) |
| ~%a~, ~%au~ | Age of the snapshot, in ~m~, ~h~ or ~d~ |

All three variables can be edited in Quick Settings, with a reset to default.

*Refreshing*: *Settings → Weather* shows the last refresh time and a *Refresh weather now* button, and says whether ~%%(org-weather)~ is used in the open document, only through ~org-agenda-files~, or nowhere. ~org-weather-refresh-interval~ also refreshes automatically: ~never~ (the default) or every ~1~, ~2~, ~4~, ~6~, ~12~ or ~24~ hours, checked at open and periodically, and only while ~%%(org-weather)~ is in use. A failed refresh keeps the cached data, which persists across restarts.

~diary-anniversary~, ~diary-cyclic~, ~diary-block~ and ~diary-date~ read their dates in the order of ~calendar-date-style~, as in Emacs: month day year by default, day month year for ~european~, year month day for ~iso~. ~%%(diary-anniversary 10 31 1948) %d years~ is the same as ~%%(org-anniversary 1948 10 31)~, whose dates are always year month day.

*** General ~<%%(sexp)>~ timestamps
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-sexp-timestamps
:END:

A ~<%%(expression)>~ goes where a plain timestamp would, in a heading's title. The expression is evaluated for each day shown, and every day it is non-nil is an occurrence. It is a matcher, not a repeater: marking the heading DONE has no effect, and it can't carry a repeater suffix. It is skipped when the heading has SCHEDULED or DEADLINE, and it never carries forward.

#+BEGIN_SRC
,* Weekly Sunrise <%%(when (org-cyclic 7 2026 8 9) (diary-sunrise))>
,* TODO Team Sync <%%(diary-float t 6 1)>
,* Water the plants <%%(org-cyclic 3 2026 1 1)>
,* Company Anniversary <%%(org-anniversary 2018 5 14)>
#+END_SRC

The evaluator is a small, safe Lisp subset, not Emacs's interpreter. Each day is evaluated on its own, with ~date~ set to that day:

- ~(when CONDITION EXPR)~: the result of EXPR if CONDITION is non-nil, otherwise no match.
- ~(and EXPR...)~, ~(or EXPR...)~, ~(not EXPR)~: as in Lisp. ~and~ yields its last value, so a string survives; ~or~ yields the first that matches. ~t~ and ~nil~ work as values, and list arguments may be quoted (~'(10 11 12)~). ~<%%(and (org-block 2026 9 1 2026 12 18) (diary-float t 1 1))>~ is the first Monday of each month, within that range.
- ~date~, ~let~, ~let*~, ~if~, ~unless~, ~cond~, ~progn~: ~date~ is the day being checked, as ~(month day year)~, so ~(car date)~ is the month, ~(cadr date)~ the day and ~(nth 2 date)~ the year. Arithmetic (~+ - * / mod % 1+ 1-~), comparison (~= /= < > <= >=~), ~zerop~, ~equal~, ~list~, ~car~, ~cdr~, ~cadr~, ~nth~, ~length~, ~memq~ and ~member~ work as in Emacs. An error (a wrong argument type, division by zero, a runaway expression) is simply no match.
- ~calendar-day-of-week~ (0 is Sunday), ~calendar-last-day-of-month~, ~calendar-leap-year-p~, ~calendar-extract-month~, ~-day~, ~-year~ and ~calendar-current-date~: ~<%%(and (= (cadr date) (calendar-last-day-of-month (car date) (nth 2 date))) (memq (calendar-day-of-week date) '(1 2 3 4 5)))>~ is the last day of each month when it is a weekday.
- ~calendar-absolute-from-gregorian~ and ~calendar-gregorian-from-absolute~ turn a date into a day count and back (day 1 is 1 January, year 1), plus ~min~, ~max~ and ~abs~. A count makes "every other week" and "N days until" rules easy: ~<%%(let ((n (- (calendar-absolute-from-gregorian '(12 25 2026)) (calendar-absolute-from-gregorian date)))) (and (>= n 0) (<= n 30) (format "%d days until Christmas" n)))>~ counts down for the 30 days before.
- ~(diary-remind SEXP DAYS)~: shows the entry on the day SEXP matches, and "Reminder: Only 3 days until ..." on the DAYS before it. ~DAYS~ is a number, a list (~'(1 3 7)~), or a negative number for every day up to it. ~%%(diary-remind '(diary-float 11 4 4) 7) Thanksgiving~ starts a week ahead. The variable ~entry~ is the text of the line, so ~(and (org-block 2026 12 20 2026 12 25) entry)~ also works.
- ~(diary-day-of-year)~, ~(diary-iso-date)~, ~(diary-julian-date)~, ~(diary-astro-day-number)~ and ~(diary-lunar-phases)~ show the day's line as Emacs words it: "Day 290 of 2026; 75 days remaining in the year", "ISO date: Day 6 of week 42 of 2026", "Julian date: October 4, 2026", "Astronomical (Julian) day number at noon UTC: 2461331.0" and, on the day of a quarter, "Full Moon 12:09am (EDT)" in this device's time zone. ~%%(diary-lunar-phases)~ also works as a body line.
- ~(today-p)~: this app's shorthand for ~(equal date (calendar-current-date))~. ~<%%(when (today-p) (diary-sunrise))>~ shows sunrise only today.
- ~(org-block Y M D Y M D)~ is an inclusive range, in either order. ~(org-date Y M D)~ takes, for each field, an integer, a list or ~t~: ~(org-date t '(10 11 12) 22)~ is the 22nd of October, November and December every year. Every date is year month day, and impossible dates match nothing.
- ~(org-class Y1 M1 D1 Y2 M2 D2 DAYNAME [SKIP-WEEK...])~: DAYNAME (0 Sunday to 6) every week between the two dates, except the listed ISO week numbers. Add ~'holidays~ to the list to skip public holidays as well: the US holidays of Emacs's ~holiday-general-holidays~ and the Christian ones (Ash Wednesday, Good Friday, Easter, Christmas). ~(calendar-check-holidays date)~ gives a day's holiday names. Hebrew, Islamic and other calendars' holidays aren't included.
- ~(org-cyclic ...)~, ~(org-anniversary ...)~ and ~(diary-float ...)~, as above, work as sub-expressions. So do the solar functions, ~(diary-day-length)~ and ~(org-weather)~, which return a formatted string; a string result becomes the displayed text ("Weekly Sunrise: 06:30 Sunrise"). ~org-contacts-anniversaries~ isn't recognized inside a sexp timestamp.
- ~(format FORMAT-STRING ARG...)~ combines string-returning functions into one line: ~<%%(when (today-p) (format "Rise %s (%s)" (diary-sunrise) (diary-civil-dawn)))>~ shows "Rise 06:30 Sunrise (06:02 Dawn)", or "Rise 06:30 (06:02)" with ~solar-hide-label~. Placeholders are ~%s~ (any value), ~%d~ (a number) and ~%%~, with an optional width such as ~%02d~, ~%5s~ or ~%-5s~; each evaluates its argument, including a nested ~format~. Extra arguments are ignored; too few give no match. A title that is only the timestamp shows the result exactly as built, with no title prefix.
- Anything else (an unknown function, a malformed expression, a bare value) is no match, never an error.

*Not included*: assignment (~setq~), ~lambda~ and ~defun~, and anything with side effects, so the Emacs manual's "pay check" example (which uses ~setq~) needs a ~let*~ rewrite. Also not implemented: alternate calendars and Hebrew observances (~diary-yahrzeit~, ~diary-rosh-hodesh~ and the rest).

*** Other agenda behavior
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-behavior
:END:

- *Completed items are excluded*, using the done keywords of the file's own ~#+TODO:~ sequence.
- *Repeating timestamps expand* for SCHEDULED, DEADLINE and title timestamps: ~<2000-01-01 Sat +1y>~ shows every year within the range displayed. A repeating SCHEDULED or DEADLINE shows only on its repeat dates, with no carry-forward or early warning between them.
- *Marking a repeating task done shifts it*, as in org: its date moves forward, ~LAST_REPEAT~ is stamped, and the TODO state returns to the first keyword. ~+N~ adds one interval to the previous date, even if that is still in the past. ~++N~ adds intervals until the date is later than now, keeping the weekday and time (a timed one can land later today). ~.+N~ counts from today, or from the current time for hours. The DONE transition is logged normally; the bounce-back is not, and the ~CLOSED~ timestamp is removed again.
- *Archived and commented headings are excluded*. A commented heading starts with ~COMMENT~ (~** COMMENT draft, not ready yet~), as in Emacs. The settings are ~org-agenda-skip-archived-trees~ and ~org-agenda-skip-comment-trees~ in [[#local-variables][Local Variables]].

A trailing tag needs a space before it (~<2000-01-01 Sat +1y> :BDAY:~), as in org. Without the space the tag stays as title text, but the timestamp still shows.

*** Habits
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: habits
:END:

A habit is an open TODO with ~:STYLE: habit~ and a repeating SCHEDULED date, as in Emacs's ~org-habit~. The agenda row gets a strip of days: 21 before today, today (outlined, ~!~) and 7 after. Blue: not yet due. Green: can be done. Yellow: last chance. Red: overdue. A ~*~ is a day it was done.

#+begin_example
,* TODO Shave
SCHEDULED: <2026-10-13 Tue .+2d/4d>
:PROPERTIES:
:STYLE: habit
:END:
#+end_example

~.+2d/4d~ means every 2 days, no later than every 4. Set the second number under Details > Dates > "No later than". Marking the habit done records a ~State "DONE"~ line in its ~:LOGBOOK:~; the strip is drawn from those lines. A habit shows in today's agenda once it is due. Settings > Agenda has ~org-habit-preceding-days~, ~org-habit-following-days~, ~org-habit-show-habits-only-for-today~ and ~org-habit-show-all-today~. The ⏱ panel hides habits for the session.

Tap a habit's strip for its history: how many times in a row it was done on time (each no later than the last-chance day after the one before), the best run, the last 12 weeks as a grid, and the latest completions. Details > Props has a *Habit* switch that sets ~STYLE: habit~.

*** Agenda Files
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-files
:END:

Add files in *Settings → Quick Settings → Agenda files*, or in a document's own ~# Local Variables:~ block to override that for the one file (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]). Entries are semicolon-separated ~scheme:path~ pairs, like ~github:journal.org;webdav:notes/todo.org~, the same syntax as ~org-refile-targets~ (see [[#refile][Refile]]). The Agenda and TODO views then scan all of them. ~github~ and ~webdav~ files are fetched; ~local:name.org~ reads a file on this device: one you have opened with *File → Open → Local file* or, in the [[#android-app][Android app]], one in the org-pwa folder. A malformed entry is skipped. If the open file is in the list, its live in-memory version is used.

Files are fetched once per session. Once any are configured, a *↻* button in the agenda controls refetches them, and a file that fails to load is reported above the list. A local file is read-only here: Agenda, TODO, Search and Export use it, but Refile, Replace and Capture never write into it. It loads only if the browser already allows access; otherwise the agenda says it "needs permission", and the *↻* button, being a tap, is what asks. Export's *This file + Agenda Files* scope always fetches fresh (see [[#export][Export]]). Two entries with the same file name, such as ~github:notes.org~ and ~local:notes.org~, can't both be used: the first is, and the agenda says so for the second.

*** Contacts Files
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: contacts-files
:END:

Set in *Settings → Quick Settings → Contacts files*, or per document in Local Variables, exactly like [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]] (real org-contacts' ~org-contacts-files~; ~github~, ~webdav~ and ~local~). [[#export][Contacts (.vcf)]] export's *This file + Contacts Files* scope scans them. The list is independent of Agenda Files, because the two commonly differ.

*** Calendar and contacts sync (CalDAV, CardDAV)
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: calendar-sync
:END:

Mirror your agenda into a calendar on your own server, so its items appear, with alarms, in your phone's calendar app. Create a calendar on the server first (a Radicale or Nextcloud calendar), then set it in *Settings → Calendar (CalDAV) / Contacts (CardDAV)*: the calendar's address, and a username and password (blank means the WebDAV ones). Leave the address blank to turn it off.

It is one-way: the calendar follows the agenda, and edits made in a calendar app are overwritten, so give it a calendar of its own. The app removes only events it created, and only for files it has loaded.

What goes in is what *View → Agenda* shows, from the open file and your [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]]: SCHEDULED, DEADLINE, plain timestamps, diary entries, and birthdays and anniversaries (from your Contacts Files). Each event has its title, its start and end time, the heading's tags as categories, its ~:LOCATION:~ and the start of its body (400 characters), and a deadline's warning delay (~-3d~) becomes an alarm. Every event with a time of day also gets an alarm ~appt-message-warning-time~ minutes before it (Settings → Agenda notifications); all-day events don't. A repeating item is one event with a repeat rule. A birthday or anniversary is one event for each year in the window, with that year's age. Completed items, and the agenda's overdue and warning-day entries, are not sent. Items are kept from a month back to six months ahead.

A ~<%%(…)>~ timestamp in a heading title becomes one all-day event for each day it matches, so ~<%%(when (today-p) (org-weather))>~ is a single event for today. It reads "Weather as of 10:45" in its description, from the last forecast fetched, and the calendar sync updates that one event whenever the weather refreshes (see ~org-weather-refresh-interval~). Yesterday's is removed. Your location, the weather settings and any script-defined functions (see [[#extensions][Extensions]]) are used just as in the Agenda; a script's functions are asked first and the export waits for the answers. Plain ~%%(diary-sunrise)~, ~%%(diary-sunset)~ and ~%%(org-weather)~ lines in a body are Agenda-only and are not exported.

It syncs after a save, when you return to the app, and at launch. *Sync* in Settings does it now, and *Rebuild calendar* (or the palette's *Rebuild calendar from the agenda*) removes the app's events and sends them all again. After a wrong address or password, automatic syncing stops until you change the settings or sync by hand.

*Contacts* work the same way. Create an address book on the server, and set its address as the *Contacts address*. It uses the same username and password as the calendar, and either address can be left blank. Your [[#contacts-files][Contacts Files]] are mirrored into it, one vCard per contact, in Flat or Tree style. The open file is not sent unless it is one of them, and a contact is removed only when its own file was loaded. *Sync* does the calendar and the contacts together, and says how each went. *Rebuild contacts* (or *Rebuild contacts from the contacts files*) removes the app's contacts and sends them all again. *Sync agenda to calendar* and *Sync contacts to the address book* do one each.

Examples: ~https://dav.example.com/radicale/me/calendar/~ and ~https://dav.example.com/radicale/me/contacts/~. As with WebDAV, the server must allow CORS requests, including ~PUT~, ~DELETE~ and ~PROPFIND~ with the ~Authorization~, ~Content-Type~ and ~Depth~ headers.

*** Agenda notifications
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: agenda-notifications
:END:

Get a reminder shortly before an appointment, as Emacs's ~appt~ does. Turn it on in *Settings → Agenda notifications*; the settings use Emacs's names and belong to this device.

- *Agenda notifications* (~appt-activate~): on or off.
- *Warn this many minutes before* (~appt-message-warning-time~): 12 by default, as in Emacs, adjustable in 1-minute steps.
- *Remind again every* (~appt-display-interval~): 3 minutes by default. Once an appointment is within its warning time, it is announced again at this interval, as in Emacs: 10 minutes warned every 3 reads 10, 7, 4 and 1. A warning time that is a multiple of the interval also ends with a reminder at the start.
- *Scan agenda files every* (~appt-agenda-scan-interval~): 5 minutes by default. The app also looks again at launch, when you return to it, and after a save.
- *Countdown in the mode line* (~appt-display-mode-line~): shows ~Appt: 10m~ while an appointment is inside its warning time.
- *Show reminders as* (~appt-display-format~): *window* is a system notification plus a banner in the app; *echo* is the status line only.

An appointment is an item with a time of day, from the open file and your [[#agenda-files][Agenda Files]]: SCHEDULED, DEADLINE or a plain timestamp, repeating ones included. Done items and items with no time of day are ignored. A reminder is titled by the appointment, with the time left and its time below: ~Dentist~, ~in 10 min · 09:30–10:15~. Under that comes the start of the heading's body (up to 400 characters), the same text the calendar sync sends; on Android it shows when the notification is expanded. The banner stays until you tap *Open day* or *Dismiss*, and the next reminder replaces it. A system notification stays until you swipe it away, and the repeats replace each other. Tapping a reminder opens that day in the Agenda.

The first time, tap *Allow notifications*. If they are blocked, reminders still show in the app. In the browser, reminders appear while the app is open. In the [[#android-app][Android app]] they are scheduled with the system, so they arrive when the app is closed; allowing *Exact timing* keeps them on the minute.

-----

** The TODO view
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: the-todo-view
:END:

Tap *View → TODO* for every active TODO-state heading in the file, whatever its dates (org's ~C-c a t~). A TODO with no date never shows in the Agenda, so this is where it lives.

It is a flat list in document order, each item showing its TODO keyword, title, category and SCHEDULED or DEADLINE date (overdue in red). The filter chips work as in the Agenda. *Sort* cycles through document order, date order (undated tasks last), least effort first and most effort first. Tap an item to jump to it in the outline; press and hold or swipe it as in the [[#agenda][Agenda]]. It has the same exclusions as Agenda (completed items, by the file's ~#+TODO:~ sequence, archived headings and commented headings, with the same [[#local-variables][Local Variables]] overrides).

*Clock report*: a checkbox beside *Clock* shows org's ~org-clock-report~ (a ~clocktable~ block) read-only instead of writing it into the document. It asks for a start and end date (the last 7 days at first) and a ~maxlevel~ (1 to 10, default 2). Each row's total includes its descendants; headings with no clocked time are omitted, and a running clock is excluded. *Copy* gives valid org dynamic-block syntax to paste into a file.

-----

** Capture Templates
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: capture-templates
:END:

The palette's *Capture* command (or ~C-c c~) opens org's ~org-capture-templates~: file a note, task or table row at a set place without navigating there. Tap a template; if it has ~%^{Prompt}~ or ~%?~ fields, a form asks for each, with a live preview of the result. A template with no prompts captures at once.

After a capture the form returns to the template list. If a capture fails (network error, sync conflict) the form keeps your text. Every template is also a palette command, *Capture: <description>*, and the Extras menu (see [[#extras-menu][Extras Menu]]) can jump to one by key.

A capture into a different file goes into that file's buffer, as in Emacs: it opens in a background tab, modified until you save it (*Save* or *Save Some Buffers*, see [[#file-management][File management]]). If the file has no tab and has unsaved local changes from an earlier session, the capture refuses; open the file, resolve them, and retry.

Four templates are the default: ~b~ (Bullet List), ~c~ (Check List), ~m~ (Meeting) and ~t~ (Table Row). Edit or replace them in *Settings → Capture Templates*, as a JSON array of template objects.

*Template shape:*

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{
  "key": "b",
  "description": "Bullet List",
  "type": "item",
  "olp": ["heading 1", "heading n"],
  "template": "%? [The captured text or note]",
  "file": "journal.org",
  "prepend": true,
  "prependHeading": true
}
#+END_SRC

- ~key~: must be unique. It is the hotkey in a god-mode picker and shows beside the description on the capture form.
- ~type~: ~item~ (a bullet), ~checkitem~ (a checkbox item), ~plain~ (raw text parsed as an org fragment; the only type that can contain headings, drawers or TODO keywords) or ~table-line~ (a row added to the nearest table under the target, or a new table).
- ~olp~: the outline path to insert into, found or created heading by heading. A segment wrapped in ~%<FORMAT>~ (like ~"%<%Y-%m>"~) expands dynamically, so a monthly table can target "2026-07" without creating that heading by hand. Other segments are literal.
- ~file~ (optional): capture into a different file (org's ~file+olp~). A bare name is a sibling of the open file, a path containing ~/~ is used as is, and an optional ~github:~, ~webdav:~ or ~local:~ prefix names the backend; a prefix that doesn't match the open document's backend is refused. If it resolves to the open file, the capture lands in that live document. Otherwise the other file is read, changed and written back without being opened, and nothing changes if the write fails. Omit it to capture into the open file. GitHub and WebDAV targets work automatically; a local or iOS-imported target must have been opened or saved once first, except in the [[#android-app][Android app]], where a file in the org-pwa folder works automatically and is created if it doesn't exist.
- ~template~: the text inserted, after %-expansion. A JSON ~\n~ is a newline; a blank line after the entry is ~"...%?\n"~.
- ~prepend~ (default ~false~): put the new entry at the top instead of the bottom. A new list item goes before the first item, and a new table row goes right after the header row and rule. For ~item~, ~checkitem~ and ~plain~ it also puts any auto-created ~olp~ heading first among its siblings.
- ~prependHeading~ (default ~false~; ~table-line~ only): put newly created ~olp~ headings first among their siblings, independently of ~prepend~. That keeps the newest month's heading on top while its rows still append in order. It applies at every level that has to be created; existing segments are reused as they are.
- ~omitEmptyEntries~ (default ~false~; ~plain~ only): remove entries whose expanded value is empty because a ~%^{Prompt}~ was left blank. That covers ~:KEY:~ drawer entries and body lines shaped ~KEY:value~, such as raw vCard lines (for ~N~ and ~ADR~, a value of only whitespace and semicolons counts as empty). It also removes an empty trailing tag (a blank ~:%^{Tag}:~ would show as ~::~), in every sub-heading the capture defines.
- ~preText~, ~postText~ (optional, default empty): template text, in the same %-language, added around the output. For ~item~, ~checkitem~ and ~plain~ it wraps every capture, with no automatic spacing. For ~table-line~ it is added once, when the target has no table yet: ~preText~, the new table with this first row, then ~postText~; later captures only add rows. No blank line separates them from the table, so a header row and rule in ~preText~ join the table, and a ~#+TBLFM:~ or ~#+PLOT:~ line is picked up (see [[#table-formulas][Table formulas]] and [[#plots][Plots]]). A ~%^{Prompt}~ in them still appears on the form even when the capture won't use it, unless the target is the open document, a loaded Agenda File or a local file, where the form can check first.

*Template text, the %-escape language* (local time):

- ~%<FORMAT>~ is a ~format-time-string~ subset. The examples use Wednesday, March 5, 2025, 14:30:07:

| Specifier | Meaning | Example output |
|---+---+---|
| ~%a~ | Abbreviated weekday name | ~Wed~ |
| ~%A~ | Full weekday name | ~Wednesday~ |
| ~%b~ | Abbreviated month name | ~Mar~ |
| ~%B~ | Full month name | ~March~ |
| ~%d~ | Day of month, zero-padded (01–31) | ~05~ |
| ~%e~ | Day of month, space-padded ( 1–31) | ~␣5~ |
| ~%F~ | ISO date (~%Y-%m-%d~ combined) | ~2025-03-05~ |
| ~%H~ | Hour, 24-hour, zero-padded (00–23) | ~14~ |
| ~%I~ | Hour, 12-hour, zero-padded (01–12) | ~02~ |
| ~%j~ | Day of year, zero-padded to 3 digits (001–366) | ~064~ |
| ~%m~ | Month, zero-padded (01–12) | ~03~ |
| ~%M~ | Minute, zero-padded (00–59) | ~30~ |
| ~%p~ | ~AM~ or ~PM~ | ~PM~ |
| ~%R~ | Hour:minute (~%H:%M~ combined) | ~14:30~ |
| ~%S~ | Second, zero-padded (00–59) | ~07~ |
| ~%T~ | Hour:minute:second (~%H:%M:%S~ combined) | ~14:30:07~ |
| ~%y~ | 2-digit year | ~25~ |
| ~%Y~ | 4-digit year | ~2025~ |
| ~%z~ | Numeric UTC offset (±HHMM); depends on the device's time zone (shown for US Eastern summer time) | ~-0400~ |
| ~%Z~ | Time zone abbreviation; device-dependent like ~%z~ | ~EDT~ |
| ~%%~ | A literal percent sign | ~%~ |

  An unrecognized specifier is left visible (~%Q~ stays ~%Q~).

- ~%t~, ~%T~: an active timestamp, date only or date and time. ~%u~, ~%U~: the same, inactive (~[...]~ instead of ~<...>~).
- ~%i~ is content shared in from another app (see [[#capture-from-other-apps][Capturing from other apps]]), and ~%a~ is a link to the shared page, ~[[url][title]]~. Text before ~%i~ on its line is added before every later line, so a ~%i~ that follows indentation keeps every line indented. A shared line that would start a heading or a ~#+~ line gets a leading comma, so shared text can never change the document's structure, and only web and mail addresses become links. Both are empty when nothing was shared.
- ~%x~ is the clipboard. It is read only for a template that uses it, the browser may ask permission (iOS shows a Paste confirmation), and a refusal leaves it empty while the capture still goes ahead.
- ~%^{Prompt}~ asks a question on the in-app form. ~%^{Prompt|default}~ pre-fills an answer, and ~%^{Prompt|default|choice1|choice2}~ also lists the choices as a hint under the field (there is no dropdown). Several prompts share one form, and cancelling discards the whole capture.
- ~%^t~, ~%^T~, ~%^u~, ~%^U~ are interactive timestamps: active date (~<2026-09-22 Tue>~), active date and time, inactive date (~[2026-09-22 Tue]~), inactive date and time. Active timestamps show in the [[#agenda][Agenda]]; inactive ones don't. Each is a text field with a *📅 Pick date* (or *📅 Pick date & time*) button. In the popup, *OK* writes the timestamp into the field, where it stays editable, and *Cancel* leaves the field as it was. The date & time popup also has an *End time*, which follows the start by 30 minutes until you change it (*No end* removes it) and writes a range such as ~<2026-09-22 Tue 09:00-10:30>~: an appointment with a start and an end, exported with both. They count as prompts, in reading order, for ~%\N~ and the live preview.
- ~%\N~ (~%\1~, ~%\2~, ...) re-inserts the answer already given to the Nth ~%^{Prompt}~ or ~%?~ (1-based) instead of asking again. Out of range gives empty text. In the JSON text the backslash must be doubled: ~%\\1~.
- ~@#~ is the table-formula row number, for ~table-line~ captures only (empty otherwise). It takes an offset, ~@# + n~ or ~@# - n~, with n a non-negative integer.
- ~%?~ is org's cursor marker, treated as one more prompt: labeled "Text", asked on the form, and focused with the keyboard up when it is the first or only field.

*Two worked examples:*

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{
  "key": "t",
  "description": "Tracking",
  "type": "table-line",
  "olp": ["🛍️ Bag - lists and notes", "❤️ Health", "🏩 Tracking", "%<%Y-%m>"],
  "preText": "#+PLOT: title:\"Tracking\" ind:4 deps:1 with:points ticks:6",
  "postText": "#+TBLFM: $4=round(trunc($3/100) + 100*($3/100 - trunc($3/100)) / 60)",
  "template": "| @# | %<%Y-%m-%d> | %<%H%M> ||",
  "prependHeading": true,
  "file": "github:home.org"
}
#+END_SRC

*Tracking* logs a value with its date and time into a table, and plots it:

- ~olp~ is four segments deep. The last, ~"%<%Y-%m>"~, creates the current month's heading the first time anything is captured that month.
- ~preText~ sets up the chart once, when the month's table is created: ~ind:4~ and ~deps:1~ plot the 4th column against the 1st (the row number) as points.
- ~postText~ sets up the formula once. It converts a raw ~HHMM~ value (~$3~, such as ~1830~) to the nearest whole hour in ~$4~: ~trunc($3/100)~ is the hour, the rest turns the minutes into a fraction, and ~round()~ rounds the sum, so 1830 gives 19, not 18.5.
- ~template~ is the one row: ~@#~, a date, an ~HHMM~ time, and a trailing ~||~ that leaves the 4th cell for the formula.
- ~prependHeading: true~ keeps the newest month's heading on top, while its rows append in order.
- ~file: "github:home.org"~ captures into that file on GitHub, whatever is open.

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{
  "key": "v",
  "description": "vCard Contact",
  "type": "plain",
  "olp": ["New"],
  "file": "github:contacts.org",
  "omitEmptyEntries": true,
  "template": "* %^{First Name} %^{Last Name} :%^{Category/Tag}:\nBEGIN:VCARD\nVERSION:3.0\nFN:%\\1 %\\2\nN:%\\2;%\\1;;;\nEMAIL:%^{Email}\nTEL;TYPE=voice:%^{Phone Number}\nTEL;TYPE=cell:%^{Mobile Number}\nADR;TYPE=home:;;%^{Street};%^{City};%^{State};%^{Postal Code};%^{Country}\nBDAY:%^{Birthday (YYYY-MM-DD)}\nNOTE:%^{Note}\nORG:%^{Company/Organization}\nTITLE:%^{Job Title}\nEND:VCARD\n\n%?"
}
#+END_SRC

*vCard Contact* builds a whole heading with a ~plain~ capture: a title with an inline tag prompt, and a raw multi-line body. ~FN:%\1 %\2~ and ~N:%\2;%\1;;;~ reuse the two name answers through backreferences instead of asking twice. The body has the shape the vCard export produces for its *new buffer* destination (see [[#export][Contacts (.vcf) export]]), which Import reads back (see [[#import][Import]]). ~omitEmptyEntries: true~ drops every blank field, and the trailing ~%?~ leaves the cursor below the vCard for a free-form note.

*** Capturing from other apps
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: capture-from-other-apps
:END:

On Android, the installed app is a share target: choose *org-pwa* in another app's Share sheet and the shared title, text and link open Capture. Pick a template; its ~%i~ and ~%a~ take the content. Long-press the app icon for a *Capture* shortcut.

The built-in *Web page or text* template is made for this. Share a web page and it files a heading under *Inbox* that links to the page, titled as the page is; leave its title prompt blank. Share some text from a document and it files the text under a heading with the title you type. Either way the second prompt takes your own note, and ~:CREATED:~ records when. A part that isn't there (no text, no note) leaves a blank line. If you already have templates of your own, add it in *Settings → Capture Templates*:

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{ "key": "w", "description": "Web page or text", "type": "plain", "olp": ["Inbox"],
  "template": "* %a%^{Title (leave blank for a web page)}\n:PROPERTIES:\n:CREATED: %U\n:END:\n  %i\n  %?", "emptyLines": 1 }
#+END_SRC

Any link or bookmark can do the same. ~index.html?capture=KEY~ runs the template with that key, a bare ~?capture~ shows the list, and ~&text=~, ~&title=~ and ~&url=~ carry content. The address is cleaned afterwards, so reloading never captures twice, and it works offline.

Example: ~index.html?capture=n&text=Buy%20milk~ with this template files the text under *Inbox*:

#+BEGIN_SRC json
{ "key": "n", "description": "Shared note", "type": "plain", "olp": ["Inbox"], "template": "* Note\n  %i\n  %a" }
#+END_SRC

A template that files into another file (~file:~) needs a document from the same backend open; the app restores your tabs when it starts.

*iPhone*: iOS can't share to installed web apps. Copy the text (a Shortcut can do it), open the app and run a template that contains ~%x~.

-----

** Extras menu
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: extras-menu
:END:

A floating ☰ button at bottom-right opens a configurable list of quick actions. It is this app's own feature, set with ~org-xx-extra-menu~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]); the button is hidden while the variable is unset. The sibling ~org-xx-menu-aliases~ relabels or hides buttons in the File, More, Export and View menus (see [[#menu-customization][Menu customization]]).

*Syntax*: a sequence of double-quoted ~"SPEC;LABEL"~ entries, spread over several lines with a trailing ~\~ (see [[#configuration][Configuration]] for line continuation). Settings → Quick Settings shows and edits it in this one-entry-per-line form (see [[#settings][Settings]]):

#+BEGIN_SRC
org-xx-extra-menu: "j;📔 Journal" \
                   "c;✅ Checklist" \
                   "m;👥 Meeting" \
                   "-----" \
                   "t;⭐ Tracking" \
                   "["🛍️ Bag - lists and notes", "❤️ Health", "🏩 Tracking", "%<%Y-%m>"];👁 Current" \
                   "-----" \
                   "'calendar;📅 Calendar"
#+END_SRC

*LABEL* is the text shown, exactly as written (icon and all). *SPEC* is one of three shapes:

- A bare *capture-template key* (~t~, ~j~, ~c~, ~m~ above) runs that template, as if picked from the Capture menu (see [[#capture-templates][Capture Templates]]). A key with no template shows a status message.
- A bracketed *OLP path*: an array of double-quoted heading titles, as in a capture template's ~olp:~, each segment expanded for ~%<FORMAT>~ when the item is tapped (~"%<%Y-%m>"~ gives the current year and month). It navigates to that heading. Unlike a capture template, it never creates a missing heading, because browsing a menu shouldn't write to the file: a path that doesn't fully exist creates nothing and says so.
- A *quoted function reference* (~'calendar~ above) runs the command palette command with that real Emacs or Org function name, as if chosen from the palette. It acts on the heading whose action menu is open, else the keyboard-focused one. A command that can't run says why in the status line (~Clock out: no clock is running.~), and no confirmation is asked, since choosing the item is the confirmation. The names are the ones the palette shows and searches (~org-clock-out~, ~org-clock-in~, ~org-refile~, ~org-todo~, ~org-agenda~, ~save-buffer~, ~isearch-forward~, ~calendar~, ~org-html-export-to-html~ and the rest), so type a function name into the palette to find the command, and quote the same name here.

  *Exceptions*: *New document* and *Undo history* have no Emacs function to name. Emacs has no dedicated new-buffer command (~switch-to-buffer~ with an unused name is the usual way, and ~scratch-buffer~ only returns to the one ~*scratch*~ buffer), and its undo history is a variable, ~buffer-undo-list~, not a command. A name that no command has shows ~'name is not a recognized function.~ when tapped; the entry stays in the menu, so a typo is visible.

  *Recalculate all tables* (~org-table-recalculate-buffer-tables~) recalculates every ~#+TBLFM:~ formula in the document as one undo step, where org's ~C-c C-c~ recalculates one table (see [[#table-formulas][Table formulas]]). *Export as an Org buffer* is ~org-org-export-as-org~ (see [[#export][Export]]).

  *The calendar* (~'calendar~, the palette's *Calendar*) is named after Emacs's command but is this app's own single-month overview, with year and month navigation and a Today jump. Today is bold with a two-colour halo ring that stays visible on any background. Each day is colour-coded by what is on it, from the same agenda pipeline the Agenda uses: green for a contact's birthday (~org-contacts-anniversaries~, see [[#agenda][Agenda]]), blue for any other event (SCHEDULED, DEADLINE, a plain timestamp or a diary-sexp entry), and burnt orange when both. Ambient daily diary entries (sunrise, sunset, weather) and logbook entries don't count, since they would colour nearly every day. Tapping a date closes the calendar and opens Agenda's Day view on that date, whatever is open or connected. The displayed month is remembered for the rest of the session.

Five hyphens (~"-----"~) on their own are a visual separator rather than an item, for grouping related actions.

A malformed entry (bad OLP JSON, an invalid function name, an unrecognized spec, a missing label) is skipped without breaking the rest of the menu.

-----

** Menu customization
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: menu-customization
:END:

~org-xx-menu-aliases~ (a Global or Local Variable; this app's own) relabels or hides buttons in the File, More, Export, Import and View menus. ~org-xx-extra-menu~ adds a quick-access menu instead (see [[#extras-menu][Extras menu]]).

*Syntax*: double-quoted ~"menu:Label;alias"~ entries, space-separated and spread over several lines with a trailing ~\~. ~menu~ is ~file~, ~more~, ~export~, ~import~ or ~view~. Settings → Quick Settings shows and edits it one entry per line (see [[#settings][Settings]]):

#+BEGIN_SRC
org-xx-menu-aliases: "more:Commands;💲 Commands" \
                     "more:Export;📤 Export" \
                     "more:Import;📥 Import" \
                     "more:Settings;⚙️ Settings"
#+END_SRC

Export and Import are steps within the More menu with their own namespaces, ~export:~ and ~import:~. A form like ~"more:export:HTML;📄"~ is read as the label ~export:HTML~ in ~more~, matches nothing, and is ignored.

~Label~ is a built-in button label (table below). An unknown label or menu is skipped; a label never mentioned keeps its default, since this is an override list.

*~alias~*, after the semicolon:

- *Non-empty*: replaces the button's visible text. The button does the same thing, and the original label becomes its accessible name (for screen readers and tooltips).
- *Empty* (~"menu:Label;"~): the button is omitted entirely. ~"export:Markdown;"~ hides the Markdown button from the Export menu. *~more:Settings~ is the exception*: it can never be hidden, because GitHub and WebDAV setup and Global Variables are reachable only from there, so an empty alias keeps the label ~Settings~.

*Order*: buttons can be reordered once every label of a menu is listed (the table has the complete sets); a partial list leaves the order alone. The buttons then follow the order written. An empty alias hides the button (except ~more:Settings~), so to keep one visible repeat its text: ~"more:Settings;Settings"~. To show More as Settings, Commands, Import, Export:

#+BEGIN_SRC
org-xx-menu-aliases: "more:Settings;Settings" "more:Commands;Commands" \
                     "more:Import;Import" "more:Export;Export"
#+END_SRC

*Popup menus*: File, View, More and Extras open as small popups next to their button. Tapping outside closes one, and choosing an action closes it with the result on the status line. All popups share Settings → Appearance → *Menu Size* (Regular or Small). Export is a step within More; *‹ Back* returns to the list.

The real labels of each menu, as used in ~"menu:Label;alias"~:

| ~menu~ | Labels |
|----------+--------|
| ~file~ | ~Export~, ~New~, ~Open~, ~Save~, ~Save As~, ~Save Some Buffers~ |
| ~more~ | ~Commands~, ~Export~, ~Import~, ~Settings~ |
| ~export~ | ~ASCII~, ~HTML~, ~LaTeX~, ~Markdown~ |
| ~import~ | ~Contacts (.vcf)~, ~iCalendar (.ics)~ |
| ~view~ | ~Agenda~, ~Org~, ~Text~, ~TODO~ |

~Save Some Buffers~ can be given an alias or hidden like the others, but it always comes last: it isn't part of a reordering list, so a File menu order you set earlier keeps working.

-----

** File management
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: file-management
:END:

*File menu*: New, Open, Save, Save As, Save Some Buffers. The 💾 button beside it is a one-tap *Save*, disabled when there is no document or nowhere to save yet.

- *New* creates a document in memory, with no picker or backend to choose. Edits are cached locally, so a crash can be resumed with the usual "resume unsaved local version" prompt. The tab shows ~*scratch*~ in the red unsaved style until the first heading gets a title, which becomes the label. *Save* stays disabled; *Save As* picks a destination. Handy as a scratch pad for trying a capture template or table formula.
- *Open* and *Save As* share one screen with a *GitHub / Local file / WebDAV* picker (*Import file* / *Download* on iOS, where a file is read once rather than linked). It opens on the type you used last. *Local file* opens your device's file picker.
- *GitHub and WebDAV show a folder listing.* Tap a folder (📁) to enter it; *↑ Up* goes back. Only ~.org~ files (📄) and ~_archive~ files (🗄️, see [[#archiving][Archiving]]) are listed. WebDAV needs ~PROPFIND~ (Nextcloud, ownCloud and Apache ~mod_dav~ have it). The *Enter path…* field opens a file by path, which also works when listing fails. A backend you haven't set up links to its settings.
- *Save* writes back to the backend the file came from, without asking again.
- *Save Some Buffers* (~save-some-buffers~, ~C-x s~) asks about each modified tab in the minibuffer: ~y~ or Space saves, ~n~ or Backspace skips, ~!~ saves this and the rest, ~.~ saves this and stops, ~q~ or Escape stops, ~d~ shows what changed. Each save is the same as *Save*. *File → Save Some Buffers* saves them all without asking; it is dimmed when nothing is modified and skips new unsaved documents.
- *Revert Buffer* (palette, ~revert-buffer~) reads the open file again and drops the buffer's unsaved changes, after asking if there are any. *Undo* brings them back.
- *Capture, Refile, Archive and Replace edit buffers, not files.* An entry sent to another file goes into that file's tab (opened in the background if needed), with the modified dot until you save. Nothing is written behind your back, and the Agenda reads the buffer. Modified buffers are also kept on the device, so closing the app doesn't lose them.
- *Line endings* are kept: a CRLF file is saved back with CRLF, so a save changes only the lines you edited.
- *Save As* picks a new destination, possibly on another backend. Browse to a folder, type a name and press Save; an existing file asks before it is replaced, and again if someone else saved it meanwhile.
- If a file has unsaved local edits when you open it, you are asked to *resume* or *discard* them; either way it opens. *Settings → Pending Local Changes* lists every file with unsynced edits, with *Discard* for each and *Discard all*.
- *Conflicts*: if the stored version changed since the last sync, Save merges the two where it safely can and asks only about the parts that clash (see [[#offline-behavior-and-sync][Offline behavior and sync]]).
- *Recently opened* lists up to five files you opened or saved (never the current one), sorted alphabetically and kept across sessions. Tap to open directly; long-press an entry to remove it, or the label to clear the list. A file brought in with *Import* (iOS) can't be reopened without selecting it again.

-----

** Tabs
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tabs
:END:

*Several documents can be open at once.* Opening a file (New, Open, Recently opened, a ~file:~, ~github:~ or ~webdav:~ link, or an Agenda or Search result) adds a tab; opening one already open switches to it. Each tab keeps its own content, cursor, scroll position, view mode and undo history (see [[#undoredo-and-history][Undo/redo and History]]).

The tab bar is always visible. Each tab shows the filename (or the first heading's title for an unsaved document) and a red dot when it has unsaved changes. Tap to switch. The × closes a tab, asking first if it is modified (as Emacs's ~kill-buffer~ does). Closing the last tab opens a fresh empty document.

The open tabs persist across restarts, each restored as left.

*Help* has its own tab (see [[#docs][Help]]), always last and styled distinctly. It stays open when you switch away but doesn't survive a restart.

-----

** Citations
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: citations
:END:

*Org-cite citations* work as in Emacs's default (~basic~) processor. Write ~[cite:@knuth84]~, ~[cite/t:@knuth84 p. 5]~ or ~[cite:see @a; @b, ch. 2]~ and point at your references with ~#+BIBLIOGRAPHY: refs.bib~ (BibTeX or CSL-JSON, read from the same place as the document, one line per file). In the outline a citation stays as typed, dimmed, and tapping a key shows its entry; a key with no entry is dotted underlined.

- Styles: default (author, year), ~/t~ (text), ~/a~ (author), ~/na~ (no author), ~/n~ (nothing printed), ~/b~ (numeric), with ~/c~ and ~/b~ variants for capitals and bare form.
- ~#+PRINT_BIBLIOGRAPHY:~ marks where the reference list goes in HTML, Markdown, ASCII, ODT and LaTeX exports. ~#+CITE_EXPORT: basic plain~ (or ~numeric~) picks the list style.
- Settings (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]): ~org-cite-global-bibliography~ (files used by every document), ~org-cite-basic-sorting-field~ and ~org-cite-basic-author-year-separator~.

-----

** Export
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: export
:END:

*More → Export* lists ASCII, HTML, LaTeX and Markdown. The other formats are palette commands (*Commands*): ODT (~org-odt-export-to-odt~), As-org (~org-org-export-as-org~), Calendar (.ics) (~org-icalendar-export-to-ics~) and Contacts (.vcf) (~org-vcard-export~); the last two open their own scope choice, and C-c C-e opens the menu. File keywords such as ~#+TITLE~ and ~#+OPTIONS:~ match case-insensitively, as in org.

*Scope*: *Choose a heading…* exports just that heading and its descendants, and every heading is listed, even folded ones. The chosen heading becomes the top level of the output. *This file* exports everything. Calendar and Contacts also offer *This file + Agenda Files* or *This file + Contacts Files* once those are configured, fetched fresh at export time. In Tree style, Contacts lists only contacts (headings with ~:KIND:~).

*** Document settings

~#+TITLE~, ~#+AUTHOR~ and ~#+DATE~ appear in a whole-document export in ASCII, HTML and ODT: a visible title with the author and date beneath it (in HTML, the date and author close the page, as in Emacs), and the format's own metadata where it has some. Markdown has none of them, as in org's ~ox-md~. A subtree export starts at its heading instead.

~#+OPTIONS:~ takes these keys, chained on one line or split across several (a later value wins):

| Key | Effect |
|---+---|
| ~toc:~ | An integer depth limit, or ~nil~ for no table of contents. Independent of ~num:~ |
| ~num:~ | Heading numbers on or off. In Markdown it switches the table of contents between an ordered and an unordered list |
| ~^:~ | Sub/superscript strictness, as ~org-use-sub-superscripts~ (see [[#local-variables][Local Variables]]); overrides it for this export |
| ~author:~, ~date:~ | Show each field or not |
| ~creator:~ | A "Generated by org-pwa" notice, off by default |

HTML export also takes these, with Org's defaults:

| Key | Effect |
|---+---|
| ~H:~ | How many heading levels are headings (3); deeper ones become list items |
| ~num:N~ | Number only the first N levels |
| ~tags:~, ~todo:~, ~pri:~ | Show tags (~not-in-toc~ leaves them out of the contents), TODO keywords, priorities (off) |
| ~p:~ | Show SCHEDULED, DEADLINE and CLOSED (off) |
| ~\n:t~ | Every line break in a paragraph is kept |
| ~-:~, ~*:~, ~e:~, ~f:~, ~stat:~ | Special strings (~--~, ~...~), emphasis, entities, footnotes and ~[1/3]~ cookies |
| ~d:~ | Drawers: ~t~, ~nil~, or a list such as ~("NOTES")~ (all but LOGBOOK) |
| ~arch:~, ~tasks:~ | Archived subtrees (title only), TODO headings (~nil~, ~todo~, ~done~) |
| ~<:~, ~title:~, ~email:~ | Timestamps, the title, the author's address |

~#+EXCLUDE_TAGS:~ (default ~noexport~), ~#+SELECT_TAGS:~, COMMENT headings, ~#+SUBTITLE:~, ~#+DESCRIPTION:~, ~#+KEYWORDS:~, ~#+LANGUAGE:~ and ~#+MACRO:~ are honoured. Other formats ignore these HTML-only keys; Markdown supports only ~toc:~ and ~num:~.

~#+INCLUDE: "path" [block-type] [language] [:lines "N-M"] [:minlevel N]~ splices another document in at export time, before the first heading or in a heading's body. In a body it nests as children of that heading, one level deeper by default; at document level it keeps its own levels. The path is read from an explicit ~github:~, ~webdav:~ or ~local:~ prefix, or else relative to the open file.

- With no block type, the file is parsed as org and its headings are spliced in (its own ~#+TITLE~ and similar keywords are not). ~:minlevel N~ shifts its top level to N.
- With a block type (~src~, ~example~, ~quote~ or ~export~, optionally with a language or backend, as in ~#+INCLUDE: "path" export html~), the raw text is wrapped in that block and placed in the body.
- ~:lines "N-M"~, ~"-M"~ or ~"N-"~ filters the text first. The end line is exclusive, as in org, despite the manual's wording.

A file that can't be found is skipped silently.

~#+HTML_HEAD:~ inserts raw HTML before ~</head>~, in HTML export only and for subtree exports too; several lines are joined in order. ~#+BEGIN_EXPORT <backend>~ ... ~#+END_EXPORT~ passes its content through unescaped when the backend matches the current format (~html~, ~ascii~, ~md~ or ~markdown~, ~odt~, where the content must already be ODF XML) and is omitted otherwise.

*Header and footer*: ~html-preamble:~ and ~html-postamble:~ in ~#+OPTIONS:~ take a quoted text, as in Emacs, placed above and below the page (~nil~ drops the postamble). In it ~%t~ is the title, ~%s~ the subtitle, ~%a~ the author, ~%d~ the date, ~%e~ the email, ~%C~ or ~%T~ when it was exported, and ~%%~ a percent sign; ~\n~ starts a new line and HTML is allowed.

#+BEGIN_SRC
#+OPTIONS: html-postamble:"Prepared by %a, %d"
#+END_SRC

For text on every printed page, such as a name and a page number, use ~page-header:~ and ~page-footer:~. Parts are separated by ~|~: three are left, centre and right, two are left and right, one is the centre. ~%p~ is the page number, ~%P~ the number of pages, and the codes above work too.

#+BEGIN_SRC
#+OPTIONS: page-footer:"%a | | Page %p of %P"
#+END_SRC

They take effect when you print or use *Print → Save as PDF* in Chrome (also on a ChromeOS laptop); Firefox and Safari ignore them. Pages get a 2 cm margin to hold them. For your own CSS, such as ~@page { @bottom-center { content: counter(page); } }~, use ~#+HTML_HEAD:~.

*** ASCII

Plain text, org's ~ox-ascii~ for the core cases. Level-1 headings are underlined with ~=~ and deeper ones indented. Paragraphs wrap at ~org-ascii-text-width~ (default 72; see Local Variables), never mid-word. A link becomes ~description (target)~. Bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are stripped, and ~code~ and =verbatim= become ~`text'~. Footnote references become ~[1]~, with their definitions under "Footnotes".

*Characters*: entities such as ~\alpha~, ~\rarr~, ~\copy~ and ~\nbsp~ are replaced by the chosen character set, as in ox-ascii. Set ~org-ascii-charset~ in Local Variables to ~ascii~ (the default), ~latin1~ or ~utf-8~. UTF-8 also turns ~--~, ~---~ and ~...~ into dashes and an ellipsis, and draws underlines, bullets, checkboxes (☑ ☐ ☒), horizontal rules and block frames with box and symbol characters. Code and verbatim text are left alone.

*Blocks*: example and source blocks and lines starting with a colon sit in a frame (drawn with ~,----~, ~|~ and ~`----~, or with box-drawing characters in UTF-8). QUOTE and VERSE blocks are set in from the margin (a quote's text is also narrower); a verse keeps its line breaks. CENTER blocks centre each line. Other special blocks, including justify-left and justify-right, are set as ordinary text, and COMMENT blocks are omitted. ~#+ATTR_ASCII:~ lines are read and ignored: ~:width~ changes nothing in Emacs 29.3's output either. Headings are numbered (1, 1.1, 2) and, with more than one heading, a "Table of Contents" comes first; ~toc:~ and ~num:~ control both.

Tables are typeset: each column is padded to its widest cell, and mostly-numeric columns are right-aligned. A row of ~<N>~ cells, like ~| <30> | <10> | <24> |~ (usually above the header), fixes each column to N characters; wider content wraps within the row, breaking at hyphens when needed. That cookie row never appears in any format's output, and only ASCII uses the widths.

Not implemented: Latin-1 and UTF-8 substitutions, ~:width~ rules and justification blocks (see [[#differences-from-emacs-org-mode][Differences from Emacs org-mode]]).

*** Markdown

GFM. Checkboxes become task-list items (~- [ ]~, ~- [x]~), tables become pipe tables, code fences keep their language, and footnotes become ~[^label]~. TODO keyword, priority and tags stay as text on the heading (~# TODO [#A] Buy milk~). Underline and sub/superscript use raw ~<u>~, ~<sub>~ and ~<sup>~.

Internal links (~[[#custom-id]]~, ~[[*Heading]]~, fuzzy titles) become GitHub-style ~#slug~ anchors: lowercase, punctuation stripped, spaces to hyphens, duplicates suffixed ~-1~, ~-2~. A link outside the exported scope, or one that doesn't resolve, stays as its literal text.

*** HTML

A complete standalone page laid out like Emacs's ~ox-html~: the title as ~h1~, top-level headings as ~h2~ in numbered outline containers, ~org-ul~, ~org-ol~ and ~org-dl~ lists whose items keep their paragraphs, sub-lists and blocks, tables with a header row (when a rule follows it), column alignment and caption, figures, and footnotes numbered in order of reference. Entities (~\alpha~, ~\rarr~), timestamps, inline source, macros, ~@@html:...@@~ snippets, special blocks (~#+BEGIN_NOTE~ becomes ~<div class="note">~), verse and center blocks, ~#+TOC: headlines~, ~tables~ and ~listings~, and ~#+ATTR_HTML:~ on tables and images all work. Source blocks are coloured for common languages. Pictures the app can read (GitHub, WebDAV, attachments) are embedded, so the file stands alone.

The CSS is print-aware (headings, tables, figures and code stay whole across pages, and long code lines wrap), so the browser's *Print → Save as PDF* is the route to PDF.

For a table of contents with page numbers, tick *Add TOC with page numbers* in Settings → Export → HTML. It fills ~org-html-head~ with the Paged.js script and a little CSS (text at 70%, the size to change if you want more or less per page), and the file needs ~#+OPTIONS: toc:2~ (or another depth). Open the exported page in Chrome, wait a few seconds for it to lay out the sheets, then print at Scale 100%. The page loads the script from the web, so it must be online when opened.

*** ODT

A standalone ~.odt~ that opens in LibreOffice, Word (with the ODF filter) and Google Docs. Headings are outline levels; bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and code use named character styles; checkboxes show as ☐ and ☑; footnotes are real, editable ODF footnotes; and internal links are bookmark references. Images are referenced by path, not embedded.

*** LaTeX

A ~.tex~ file that compiles with ~pdflatex~, ~xelatex~ or ~lualatex~, laid out the way Emacs's ~org-latex-export-to-latex~ lays it out: sections, lists, tables (with ~#+ATTR_LATEX:~), figures, footnotes, citations, links, math and source blocks. When the document links pictures this app can read (GitHub, WebDAV, attachments), the export is a ~.zip~ with the pictures in ~images/~ beside the ~.tex~; otherwise it is the ~.tex~ alone. The palette command is ~org-latex-export-to-latex~. Settings → Export → LaTeX also has *Fix wide TOC numbers*, which adds the ~tocloft~ lines that keep section numbers such as 1.11.1 from running into their titles in the PDF's table of contents.

~#+LATEX_CLASS:~ (~article~, ~report~ or ~book~), ~#+LATEX_CLASS_OPTIONS:~, ~#+LATEX_COMPILER:~ and ~#+LATEX_HEADER:~ are read from the file. Settings → Export → LaTeX sets the class and compiler for files that do not. Not included: Beamer, ~minted~ or ~listings~ source blocks (code is exported as ~verbatim~) and other document classes.

*** As-org

Org's ~org-org-export-as-org~: a fully processed copy of the document in a new unsaved buffer named ~*Org ORG Export*~, leaving the original untouched. Whole document only. It:

- resolves ~#+INCLUDE:~ lines;
- expands ~{{{macro}}}~ references: ~#+MACRO: name text~ with ~$1~, ~$2~ arguments, written ~{{{name(arg1,arg2)}}}~ with ~\,~ for a literal comma, plus ~{{{title}}}~, ~{{{author}}}~, ~{{{email}}}~, ~{{{date}}}~ and ~{{{date(FORMAT)}}}~ (FORMAT applies only when ~#+DATE:~ is a single well-formed timestamp), ~{{{time(FORMAT)}}}~ and ~{{{keyword(NAME)}}}~;
- drops ~:noexport:~ headings with their subtrees, and strips ~#+BEGIN_COMMENT~ blocks and comment lines (those starting with ~#~ and a space);
- shifts the top level to 1.

Not implemented: running source blocks, and macros whose text starts with ~(eval~. Both are left as written (see Differences from Emacs org-mode). In an Extras entry it is ~'org-org-export-as-org~.

*** Calendar (.ics)

Every dated item as an iCalendar file for any calendar app: SCHEDULED, DEADLINE, plain active title timestamps and [[#agenda][org-contacts-anniversaries]]. It follows the Agenda's exclusions (archived, commented and completed headings). Re-exporting gives the same event IDs, so a calendar app updates events instead of duplicating them.

*To*: the file is downloaded. *To: file* opens the share sheet instead, which on an iPhone has *Save to Files* (a downloaded .ics there goes straight to Calendar); *To: new buffer* leaves the text in a new buffer.

*Scope*: *This file*, *Choose a heading…* and *This file + Agenda Files* write every dated item, with no window. *Agenda (as displayed)*, the last row, writes what [[#calendar-sync][the calendar sync]] sends: what View → Agenda shows, from a month back to six months ahead.

| Org source | vCalendar field | Notes |
|---+---+---|
| SCHEDULED | ~DTSTART~, ~SUMMARY~ (~DESCRIPTION~ "Scheduled") | |
| DEADLINE | ~DTSTART~, ~SUMMARY~ (~DESCRIPTION~ "Deadline") | A warning suffix (~-3d~) also becomes a ~VALARM~ reminder |
| Plain active title timestamp | ~DTSTART~, ~SUMMARY~ | Only when the heading has no SCHEDULED or DEADLINE |
| A repeater (~+1w~, ~++3d~, ~.+1m~) on any of these | ~RRULE~ | The calendar app expands the recurrence |
| A time range (~09:00-10:15~) | ~DTEND~ | |
| A heading's tags | ~CATEGORIES~ | |
| ~:LOCATION:~ | ~LOCATION~ | |
| The start of the body | ~DESCRIPTION~ | At most 400 characters |
| org-contacts-anniversaries | ~DTSTART~ with a yearly ~RRULE~, ~SUMMARY~ (~Birthday: Name~) | One yearly event cannot carry an age, so the date is in the description |

*** Contacts (.vcf)

vCard 3.0 for any contacts app, modeled on [[https://github.com/pinoaffe/org-vcard][org-vcard]] (compatible with org-contacts.el). [[https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6350][RFC 6350]] requires only ~FN~, so no email address is needed. There are two styles, and *Tree* is the default:
